# How to Re-Issue a Tax Receipt (Tax Receipts Report)

Tax receipts can be **re-issued** , **issued** , **voided** , **re-sent** and/or **downloaded** on a transaction-by-transaction basis within the **Tax Receipts Report**of your CrowdChange site. Additionally, you can download either a ZIP archive containing all PDF tax receipts within your date range and filters set, or an Excel Tax Receipts Report.

To access this report, follow these simple steps:

1. Go to your CrowdChange site and **Log In**.

2. Click **Profile** in in the top right corner, then**Admin**.

3. Go to **Reports** **\> Tax Receipts Report**using the left sidebar. You will be taken here:

   ![taxreceiptsreport.png](../assets/how-to-re-issue-a-tax-receipt-tax-receipts-report/taxreceiptsreport.png)
4. If you are looking for a specific tax receipt, you can use the search bar to search by **Donor Name** , **Email** ,**Tax Receipt Number** , or **Transaction ID**.

5. Clicking the **Filters** button allows you to filter for a specific **Time Period** , **Organization** , **Subsite** or **Fundraiser** using their respective dropdown menus. Be sure to click **Show results** to apply these filters.

   ![show results2.png](../assets/how-to-re-issue-a-tax-receipt-tax-receipts-report/show_results2.png)
6. Once you've found your desired tax receipt, click on it, then click **Re-Issue Tax Receipt**.

   ![re-issue.png](../assets/how-to-re-issue-a-tax-receipt-tax-receipts-report/re-issue.png)
7. Enter the updated information as required and click **Reissue**.

   ![reissue5.png](../assets/how-to-re-issue-a-tax-receipt-tax-receipts-report/reissue5.png)
   (You can also scroll down to adjust the Amount total and Amount benefit.)

Re-issuing a tax receipt will **VOID** the original receipt. This will be indicated within your tax receipts report and a **VOID**stamp will be added to the PDF copy of the original receipt.

The donor will receive notification of this and the re-issued receipt (sent to the email address entered when filling out the new info) will communicate that it is a replacement for the original receipt.  
Click the **Download** button to download either a ZIP archive containing all PDF tax receipts within your date range and filters set, or an Excel Tax Receipts Report.

# Optional - Tax Receipt Designation at Checkout

If you would like to give your donors the ability to designate (at checkout) to whom or which organization the tax receipt should be issued, we offer this functionality optionally on special request.  
Please note that this feature is not enabled by default - Feel free to reach out to your Partner Success Representative to discuss and request it be enabled on your site.

For fundraisers where tax receipting is enabled, enabling this feature adds a new section at checkout to ensure tax receipts are issued with the correct information. Donors will be prompted to choose from a dropdown whether the tax receipt will be issued to themselves, an organization or another individual.  
![choose.png](../assets/optional-tax-receipt-designation-at-checkout/choose.png)

Selecting **Organization** or **Another individual**will bring up additional fields in order to enter the relevant party's full name, email and billing information for the tax receipt.  
![image-20230630-163324.png](../assets/optional-tax-receipt-designation-at-checkout/image-20230630-163324.png)

# Admin > General Settings

**General Settings**is where you can adjust the inner workings of your CrowdChange site, for example:

Donations List settings, Default Fundraiser Order, Credit Card statement descriptors, Tax Receipt minimum amounts, Fundraiser Approval settings and more.

To access **General Settings**:

1. Log In to a CrowdChange account with Admin permissions.

2. Click **Profile → Admin** in the upper right-hand corner of the site. You will be taken to **General Settings**.

![image-20250722-151231.png](../assets/admin-general-settings/image-20250722-151231.png)

On the General Settings page, you will have the ability to do the following:

1. Select your **Time Zone**. Once completed, your site will operate in the Time Zone selected.

2. **Default Fundraiser Order**- This dropdown lets you choose how fundraisers are sorted by default when the home page loads. The sort order will still be changeable from the top of the homepage.

3. You can **Cap Covered Fees** so that covered fees on donations are limited to a set dollar amount.

4. **Set a minimum amount for issuing tax receipts**- This decision should be made by your organization, as entering an amount here will set it across all fundraisers within your CrowdChange site. If you wish to decide on a fundraiser-by-fundraiser basis, leave this disabled and you will be prompted to do so when creating your fundraiser.

5. **Remove from tax eligibility** - This feature allows you to disable tax eligibility for specific purchase options (eg. Tickets \& Registrations). This will remove the Expense field from the selected purchase options (shown when they are created at the fundraiser level) and their costs will never be added to the tax-eligible amount on tax receipts.

6. **Set minimum amount of recurring donation** - This allows you to set a minimum donation amount for recurring donations across all fundraisers on your site.

7. **Fundraiser Goal is Required**- This toggle allows you to set whether Fundraiser Goals are mandatory for fundraisers created on the site.

8. **Require Fundraiser Approval**- This means that any fundraiser created on your CrowdChange site must first be 'Approved' by an Admin user before it becomes active.

9. **Users can start fundraisers only from templates** - This option is only shown when **Master Templates** is enabled in General Settings

![image-20250722-151450.png](../assets/admin-general-settings/image-20250722-151450.png)
Example of General Settings

If you are viewing this section on a sub-site (child site), you will have the following option as well:  
![image-20230717-164256.png](../assets/admin-general-settings/image-20230717-164256.png)

This dropdown allows you to determine if sub-site fundraisers are mirrored to parent sites.

There are 3 options available within the dropdown:

* Fundraiser chooses - default option - this is decided per-fundraiser in fundraiser settings.

* Never - sub-site created fundraisers are never mirrored to parent sites.

* Always - sub-site created fundraisers are always mirrored to parent sites.

## E-mail Settings

Here you can customize the footer text of the automated emails sent from your CrowdChange site. Specifically, you can enter custom text for the 'From' field and the Email Signature.  
![image-20250722-151851.png](../assets/admin-general-settings/image-20250722-151851.png)  
Click the **Save**button at the bottom of the page to confirm your changes.  
![image-20231030-140928.png](../assets/admin-general-settings/image-20231030-140928.png)  
**Please Note:** You can return to the General Settings page at any time to update your configuration.

# Admin > Layout Settings

Within the Admin menu, **Layout Settings**contains 3 sub-pages for adjusting the finer details of your site:

* **Header \& Footer**- Set your site logo, logo link, menu settings, and footer settings.

* **Meta \& Analytics** - Set your site name, meta description, meta image, and analytics connectors.

* **Theme Settings**- Set your site colours and fonts.

## How to Access Layout Settings

1. Log In to a CrowdChange account with Admin permissions.

2. Click **Profile → Admin** in the upper right-hand corner of the site. You will be taken to **General Settings**.

3. On the left sidebar, click **Layout Settings**, and select one of the three sub-pages.

   ![layout.png](../assets/admin-layout-settings/layout.png)

### Header \& Footer Page

On the Header \& Footer page, you can do the following:

1. Upload a **Logo** to appear in the top-left hand corner of your CrowdChange site.

   ![image-20250722-152355.png](../assets/admin-layout-settings/image-20250722-152355.png)
   Example of Header settings
2. Add a **Logo Link** to redirect users to a certain webpage when the logo is clicked.

3. Add additional header menu links within **Menu Settings**.

4. Adjust footer information within **Footer Settings**.

Ensure to click **Save**at the bottom to confirm your changes.

### Meta \& Analytics Page

On the Meta \& Analytics page, you can do the following:

1. Edit the **Site Name** - This can be changed at any time.

   ![image-20250722-152637.png](../assets/admin-layout-settings/image-20250722-152637.png)
2. Edit the **Meta Description** and**Meta Image** which will appear across your Social Media Accounts.

   ![image-20250722-152709.png](../assets/admin-layout-settings/image-20250722-152709.png)
3. Enter your **Google Tracking ID** , **Google Tag Manager** , **Facebook Pixel ID** and **Facebook Meta Tag Domain Verification**. This is optional, however, if your organization uses any of these analytics programs, we suggest entering the account details here.

See also [**Analytics Connectors**](https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/Analytics-Connectors.1997897747.html), to learn more.

### Theme Settings Page

On the Theme Settings page, you can do the following:

1. Set your **Primary** site colour - this is the main colour used for borders, buttons, links, progress bars and form controls (e.g. checkboxes, radio buttons \& select boxes).

   ![image-20250722-152902.png](../assets/admin-layout-settings/image-20250722-152902.png)
   Example of Primary site colours
2. Set your Header background colour.

3. Set your Header Bar Background colour.

4. Set your Header Text colour.

5. Set your Footer Background colour.

6. Set your Footer Text colour.

7. Choose your **Font**.

   1. If desired, you can also click '**Advanced settings**' to import a custom font.

# How to Set Up 'In Support Of' Options

**'In Support Of' options**briefly explain the cause of a fundraiser to the general public.

For example, "In Support Of Cancer Research". Admin users have the ability to pre-set 'In support of' options which fundraiser creators on their site may choose from.  
The 'In Support of' field can also be free-text format. This depends on the configuration of your site.

'In Support of' options are displayed on both:

* The**fundraiser tile**(on the home page)...

  ![jackie.png](../assets/how-to-set-up-in-support-of-options/jackie.png)
* ...and the **Main Fundraising Page** itself, underneath the title of the fundraiser.

  ![aa6c21f0-c52b-4c96-b733-a051e242179e.png](../assets/how-to-set-up-in-support-of-options/aa6c21f0-c52b-4c96-b733-a051e242179e.png)

## Setting up 'In support of' options

To add 'In Support of' options, follow the steps below:

1. **Log In** to your CrowdChange site.

2. Click **Profile** → **Admin** in the top right corner.

3. Go to **Fundraisers Settings** **→ In support of** on the left sidebar.

4. Enter the **Name** and **Custom ID** for each option you would like to have and click **Add**.

   ![insupportoptions.png](../assets/how-to-set-up-in-support-of-options/insupportoptions.png)
   Example Options

## Editing 'In support of' options

1. Click on the **pencil icon** next to the option you want to update.

2. Make any necessary changes and click the **green tick icon**.

## Deleting 'In support of' options

1. Click on the **trash can**icon next to the option you want to delete.

2. In the popup that appears, click **Yes**.

An 'In support of' option which has been previously used by a fundraiser can be restored after being deleted by clicking the **green return arrow icon** next to said option.  
**Personal and Team Pages** also display 'In Support of' options, and depending on the settings of your site, personal page owners may or may not be able to select their 'In Support of' option of choice.

# How the Organizations Feature Works

If your charity segments its fundraising regionally or has multiple groups operating under one umbrella, the **Organizations** feature is a great way to ensure that your back-end reporting reflects this, while still allowing all donations to flow to the same holistic source.

**Organizations**is a feature that must be enabled site-wide and can be enabled by a CrowdChange support admin at any time. This feature allows users to select their organization when creating a fundraiser.

Once enabled, **Organizations** can be added from the admin menu (**Profile → Admin → Organizations**).  
![ORGANIZATIONS.png](../assets/how-the-organizations-feature-works/ORGANIZATIONS.png)

There is no limit to the number of Organizations you can add. The **Custom ID**field is used to create a shorthand identifier for reporting purposes.

With this feature enabled, when creating a fundraiser, a user will be prompted to select their organization. Using the Admin menu, site-wide administrators are able to set a default Organization if there is a specific one that is used more than the others.  
![org select.png](../assets/how-the-organizations-feature-works/org_select.png)

Once a fundraiser is live on your CrowdChange site, when using the Organizations feature, the fundraiser card will indicate at the bottom which Organization is running the fundraiser.  
![cards.png](../assets/how-the-organizations-feature-works/cards.png)
Organization shown on Fundraiser Cards on site home page  
**Admin Reports** can be filtered by Organization to allow for easier sorting and data analysis.  
The **Site-Level Access Manager** can be used in conjunction with the **Organizations** feature, allowing a Site-Wide administrator to set administrative permissions for new or existing CrowdChange users across specific Organizations within your CrowdChange site. See our article on the [**Site-Level Access Manager**](how-to-use-the-site-level-access-manager.md)

last_modified: '2026-08-12T13:45:20.621Z'

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/how-donation-matching-works | Nav: How Donation Matching Works | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# How Donation Matching Works

Donation Matching allows your organization to match eligible donations using one or more sponsor-funded matching pools.

Each sponsor can have its own:

* Available matching funds

* Availability period

* Matching multiplier

* Minimum eligible donation

* Optional maximum match per donation

When you add multiple sponsors, they are placed in a queue. CrowdChange uses the first sponsor in the queue that is currently eligible to provide the match.  
![image-20260812-134030.png](../assets/how-donation-matching-works/image-20260812-134030.png)
View of donation bar with a 2x match enabled

## Set up Donation Matching

During fundraiser creation, Donation Matching can be enabled under **Advanced Features**.

For an existing fundraiser:

1. Go to your fundraiser and log in.

2. Click **Dashboard**.

3. Select **Donation Settings** from the left sidebar.

4. Open **Donation Matching**.

5. Turn on Donation Matching.

![image-20260812-132902.png](../assets/how-donation-matching-works/image-20260812-132902.png)
View of **Donation matching settings** with **Enable** button highlighted

Once Donation Matching is enabled, add your first sponsor.

For each sponsor, enter the following information:

* **Sponsor name:** The name that identifies the sponsor, such as Company X or The Smith Family.

* **Sponsor funds:** The total amount the sponsor has made available for matching.

* **Availability:** Choose whether the sponsor remains available until its funds are used, or set a specific start and stop date.

* **Matching rules:** Set the matching multiplier, minimum eligible donation, and an optional maximum match per donation.

For example, a minimum eligible donation can be used when only donations above a certain amount should be matched. A maximum match per donation limits the amount of sponsor funds that can be applied to one donation.  
![image-20260812-133002.png](../assets/how-donation-matching-works/image-20260812-133002.png)
View of how to add a **Sponsor** within **Donation matching settings**  
![image-20260812-133048.png](../assets/how-donation-matching-works/image-20260812-133048.png)
Rules set up for a **Sponsor**

Complete the sponsor setup and save your changes.

You can add additional sponsors as needed. The order of the sponsors determines which eligible sponsor will be used first.

## Understand sponsor statuses

Each sponsor will have one of the following statuses:

* **Upcoming:** The sponsor's start date has not yet arrived.

* **Active:** The sponsor is within its availability period, has funds remaining, and has not been manually completed or archived.

* **Completed:** The sponsor's funds have been used, its end date has passed, or an administrator has manually completed it.

* **Archived:** The sponsor is retained for historical reporting but cannot match new donations.

![image-20260812-133139.png](../assets/how-donation-matching-works/image-20260812-133139.png)

The combined matching pool provides a summary of the funds across all sponsors. Each individual sponsor card shows its own total funds, used funds, remaining funds, and donation count.

## How the sponsor queue works

When a donation is eligible for matching, CrowdChange checks the sponsors in their displayed order. The first sponsor that is currently eligible provides the match.

A single donation is not split between two sponsors.

For example, assume Sponsor 1 has $40 remaining and the next donation would normally receive a $100 match. Sponsor 1 will provide its remaining $40. Sponsor 2 will be considered for the next eligible donation, but it will not provide the remaining $60 for the same donation.

When a sponsor runs out of funds, CrowdChange automatically selects the next eligible sponsor for later donations.

Administrators can also manually complete the current sponsor to advance the queue. A manually completed sponsor remains completed until it is explicitly reactivated. It can only be reactivated while:

* Its availability dates are still valid

* It has funds remaining

![image-20260812-133223.png](../assets/how-donation-matching-works/image-20260812-133223.png)
View of multiple sponsors within **Donation matching settings**  
![image-20260812-133246.png](../assets/how-donation-matching-works/image-20260812-133246.png)

### Example: sponsors with separate availability periods

Assume the following sponsors have been configured:

* Sponsor 1 is available from August 1 to August 31.

* Sponsor 2 is available from September 1 to September 30.

If Sponsor 1 runs out of funds on August 20, matching pauses until Sponsor 2 becomes eligible on September 1. September funds are not used during August.

If Sponsor 2 has an overlapping availability period, or is available immediately, the next eligible donation will use Sponsor 2 as soon as Sponsor 1 is exhausted or manually completed.

If Sponsor 1 still has unused funds when its availability period ends, those funds remain visible in Sponsor 1's history. They are not transferred to Sponsor 2.

## Reorder sponsors

You can change the order of sponsors to control which eligible sponsor is considered first for future donations.

Reordering sponsors:

* Changes the matching priority for future donations

* Does not change the sponsor associated with previous donations

* Does not move historical matching activity between sponsors

![image-20260812-133357.png](../assets/how-donation-matching-works/image-20260812-133357.png)
Click and drag sidebar to reorder sponsors

## Set up matching for teams and personal pages

For peer-to-peer fundraisers, go to:

**Donation Settings → Team \& Page Matching Setup**

When team and personal page matching is turned **off**, donations made through teams and personal pages use the fundraiser's main matching program.

When team and personal page matching is turned **on**:

* The fundraiser's main matching pool applies only to donations made directly to the fundraiser.

* Each team or personal page can have its own sponsors, sponsor queue, availability periods, and matching rules.

* A donation made through a team uses that team's matching program.

* A donation made through a personal page uses that page's matching program.

* If the team or personal page does not have an eligible sponsor, the donation is not matched using the fundraiser's main pool.

![image-20260812-133505.png](../assets/how-donation-matching-works/image-20260812-133505.png)
Click **Team \& Page donation matching setup** to enable **Donation matching**for peer-to-peer pages  
![image-20260812-133609.png](../assets/how-donation-matching-works/image-20260812-133609.png)
Once enabled, the **Team \& page matching setup**dashboard will be visible

Match pools are added via the **Team** or **Personal page dashboards** - once matching funds are added, they will be visible in the **Connected teams \& pages** list shown above.

Use the **Teams** and **Personal Pages** tabs to locate a specific team or page and open its matching setup.

The same sponsor queue rules apply at each level. Only one eligible sponsor is used for a donation, one donation is not split across multiple sponsors, and the next eligible sponsor is automatically selected for later donations.

### Team and personal page example

Assume the fundraiser has the following matching pools:

* A $10,000 general fundraiser sponsor

* A $2,000 sponsor for Team A

* A $500 sponsor for Jane's personal page

In this example:

* A donation made directly to the fundraiser uses the $10,000 general pool.

* A donation made through Team A uses Team A's $2,000 pool.

* A donation made through Jane's personal page uses Jane's $500 pool.

If Jane's sponsor funds are exhausted, later donations through Jane's page will not be matched unless another eligible sponsor is added to Jane's queue. Those donations do not fall back to Team A's pool or the fundraiser's general pool.

## Refunds and returned matching funds

When refunding a donation that received matching funds, you can choose whether the associated match should become available again.

To return the matching funds:

1. Open the fundraiser's **Donations Report**.

2. Locate the donation and click on it to get to the **Transaction details page**

3. Scroll down and click **Refund**

4. You then can determine the amount of funds to return to the match pool (see below).

5. Complete the refund.

![image-20260812-134141.png](../assets/how-donation-matching-works/image-20260812-134141.png)

This option is separate from the money being returned to the donor. It updates the matching balance associated with the donation.

When you choose to return funds to the match pool:

* The matched amount is returned to the sponsor pool that originally funded the donation.

* A partial refund returns only the matching amount associated with the refunded portion.

* Matches from team or personal page donations return to the original team or personal page pool.

When this option is left blank or set to $0:

* The donor refund is processed.

* The matched amount remains recorded as used.

Returned funds follow the original sponsor allocation. They are not added to whichever sponsor is active at the time of the refund.

### Example: refund after the active sponsor has changed

Assume Sponsor 1 matched a donation in August and later ran out of funds. Sponsor 2 then became active in September.

If the August donation is refunded in October and **Return matched funds to available matching pool** is selected, the matched funds return to Sponsor 1. They are not added to Sponsor 2.

What happens after the funds are returned depends on Sponsor 1's status:

* If Sponsor 1 was automatically completed because its funds were exhausted, and its dates are still valid, the returned funds may make it eligible again. The normal sponsor order determines when it resumes matching.

* If Sponsor 1 was manually completed, it remains completed until an administrator reactivates it.

* If Sponsor 1's availability period has ended, it remains unavailable even though its history shows remaining funds.

* If Sponsor 1 was archived, it remains archived. The funds are still credited to the correct historical pool, but the sponsor must be restored and reactivated before those funds can be used again.

For purchases containing both a direct donation and registrations, returned matching is applied to the direct donation portion first. It is then applied to registration portions in a consistent order.

## Monitor Donation Matching activity

Use the Donation Matching report to monitor and reconcile sponsor activity. This report is accessible at the fundraiser level, within the **Fundraisers report** in the reports tab of the fundraiser dashboard.

The report can help you review:

* Total sponsor funds

* Funds already used

* Remaining funds

* Number of matched donations

* Matching funds returned through refunds

![image-20260812-134454.png](../assets/how-donation-matching-works/image-20260812-134454.png)

The combined matching pool summarizes overall sponsor funding and usage.

## Important notes

* Date-based availability must have a stop date that occurs after the start date.

* A donation cannot be split between two sponsor pools.

* Editing, completing, reordering, or archiving a sponsor does not change the sponsor associated with past donations.

* Unused funds are not transferred automatically between sponsors.

* When team and personal page matching is enabled, their donations do not fall back to the fundraiser's main matching pool.

* The Donation Matching report is the best place to reconcile sponsor usage and matching funds returned through refunds.

================================================================================

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/how-pledging-works | Nav: How Pledging Works | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# How Pledging Works

CrowdChange is equipped with **Pledging** functionality, allowing you to send a direct payment link to your donors via Email or SMS, so they can pay the pledge online. This link is fundraiser-specific and you can set the amount that your donor has committed to pay. This can be done using the **Offline Donations**page.

Please see the following steps to use this functionality:

1. Go to your CrowdChange fundraiser while logged in, and click **Manage Fundraiser**(Manage my page or Manage my team on P2P pages).

2. On the left sidebar, click **Offline Donations**.

3. Once on the **Offline Donations** page, click **Add Donation**.

4. Within **General Information**, enter your donor's first and last name, email address, and donation amount.

   1. If you would like to send the payment link via **Email** , click the checkbox under Email that says '**Send link for individual or group to make online payment**'. This will send your donor the payment link directly to their email address.

   2. If you would like to send the link via **SMS**, leave this box unchecked, and once the donation has been added, you will be able to click 'Share Payment Link' and send to a Phone Number.

      ![image-20231030-165621.png](/__attachments/a_bbf255778251fa98785aaacc7a3029bd2367a8bbd2d4cecccd35cb1175e3fd16/image-20231030-165621.png?cb=1092959d618cec517305c59000394cc3)
5. If a tax receipt is desired for this donation, within Tax Receipt Information, enable **Request tax receipt for this donation** and enter the donor's address \& postal code.

   ![image-20231030-165930.png](../assets/how-pledging-works/image-20231030-165930.png)
6. To assign the donation to a team or personal page, change the date of donation, payment method, display name, show/hide amount setting, comment and add notes, click **Show Advanced Settings** within **Additional Information**.

   ![image-20231030-170259.png](../assets/how-pledging-works/image-20231030-170259.png)
7. Click **Save** at the bottom to confirm. **DO NOT** check 'Mark as received'.

   ![image-20231030-170354.png](../assets/how-pledging-works/image-20231030-170354.png)

## How to Re-send a Pledge Payment Link

If you need to re-send a payment link to a Pledge you have already entered in Offline Donations, this can be done using the following steps:

1. Go to your CrowdChange fundraiser while logged in, and click **Manage Fundraiser**.

2. On the left sidebar, click **Offline Donations**.

3. Find the donation that you would like to send a payment link for and click on it to get to the **Edit Donation** menu.

4. At the bottom of the page, click on **Share Payment Link**. You will be able to send via Email or SMS.

   ![sharelink.png](../assets/how-pledging-works/sharelink.png)

If your fundraiser has **Tax Receipts** enabled, you can include your donor's Billing Address while entering their pledge. Tax Receipts can also be issued at a later date if you don't have this information, using the [**Tax Receipts Report**](how-to-re-issue-a-tax-receipt-tax-receipts-report.md)**.**  
In a Pledging scenario, donors **do not** have the option to cover any transaction fees (Credit Card or CrowdChange platform fees) associated with the transaction.

# Image Size Guidelines

When uploading images on CrowdChange, note that **.PNG** and **.JPG**are the preferred file types, and you can see our size guidelines for each image below:  

|          **Image**          | **Recommended Image Size** | **Aspect Ratio** |
|-----------------------------|----------------------------|------------------|
| Site Logo                   | 400 x 120 pixels           | 2:1              |
| Meta Image                  | 1200 x 627 pixels          | 2:1              |
| Tax Receipt Logo Image      | 500 x 150 pixels           | 16:9             |
| Tax Receipt Signature Image | 500 x 150 pixels           | 16:9             |
| Fundraiser Cover Image      | 640 x 320 pixels           | 2:1              |
| eCards \& Tribute Cards     | 1280 x 720 pixels          | 16:9             |

## New UI / Fundraiser Redesign - Hero Block Image Sizes

| **Hero Block Style** | **Recommended Image Size** | **Aspect Ratio** |
|----------------------|----------------------------|------------------|
| Full Screen          | 1920 x 699 pixels          | 640:233          |
| Centered             | 1228 x 420 pixels          | 307:105          |
| Side                 | 528 x 500 pixels           | 132:125          |

Including text information in Hero images goes against SEO and accessibility best practices.

This information should be within the text body of the page, so that search engines can find the pages and accessibility tools (e.g. screen readers) can operate correctly.

For further details on Hero images and responsive design best practices, please refer to the following article: <https://www.optimizely.com/optimization-glossary/hero-image/>

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/analytics-connectors | Nav: Analytics Connectors - Google Analytics, Google Tag Manager, Facebook/Meta Pixel, Reddit, Pinterest, & TikTok | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# Analytics Connectors - Google Analytics, Google Tag Manager, Facebook/Meta Pixel, Reddit, Pinterest, & TikTok

CrowdChange supports integrations with several analytics and advertising platforms, allowing organizations to track website activity, campaign performance, and completed transactions.

Analytics connectors can be configured to support both browser-based tracking (Pixels, Tags, and Analytics IDs) and server-side conversion tracking (Conversions APIs and Measurement Protocol integrations), helping improve attribution accuracy and conversion reporting.

## Accessing Analytics Connectors

To access your analytics settings:

1. Log in to your CrowdChange site with an Admin account.

2. Click **Profile → Admin**.

3. Select **Layout Settings** from the left sidebar.

4. Scroll to the **Meta \& Analytics** section.

5. Enter the desired IDs, tags, verification values, or access tokens.

6. Click **Save**.

*** ** * ** ***

## Google Analytics

### Google Analytics 4 Tracking ID

The Google Analytics 4 Tracking ID connects your CrowdChange site to your Google Analytics property and enables visitor and event tracking.

Example:

`G-XXXXXXXXXX`

#### Finding Your GA4 Measurement ID

1. Open Google Analytics.

2. Navigate to **Admin → Data Streams**.

3. Select your website data stream.

4. Copy the **Measurement ID**.

*** ** * ** ***

### GA4 Measurement Protocol API Secret

The Measurement Protocol API Secret allows CrowdChange to send completed transaction events directly to Google Analytics from CrowdChange's servers.

Server-side tracking can improve attribution accuracy and help ensure completed transactions are recorded even when browser-side tracking is unavailable.

#### Creating an API Secret

1. Open Google Analytics.

2. Navigate to **Admin → Data Streams**.

3. Select your website stream.

4. Under **Measurement Protocol API Secrets**, create a new secret.

5. Copy the generated value into CrowdChange.

*** ** * ** ***

## Google Tag Manager

Google Tag Manager allows organizations to deploy custom tracking and marketing tags without modifying website code.

Separate GTM containers may be configured for English and French versions of a site.

Example:

`GTM-XXXXXXX`

### Finding Your GTM Container ID

1. Open Google Tag Manager.

2. Select your container.

3. Copy the Container ID displayed near the top of the workspace.

*** ** * ** ***

## Meta (Facebook) Analytics

### Facebook Pixel ID

The Facebook Pixel tracks visitor activity and conversion events generated through Meta advertising campaigns.

#### Finding Your Pixel ID

1. Open Meta Events Manager.

2. Select your Pixel.

3. Copy the Pixel ID displayed under your Data Source settings.

*** ** * ** ***

### Meta Conversions API Access Token

The Meta Conversions API Access Token allows CrowdChange to send completed transaction events directly to Meta from the server.

Server-side tracking improves attribution accuracy and helps Meta deduplicate events received through both the Pixel and Conversions API.

#### Generating an Access Token

1. Open Meta Events Manager.

2. Select your Pixel.

3. Navigate to **Settings**.

4. Locate the **Conversions API** section.

5. Generate an Access Token.

6. Copy the token into CrowdChange.

*** ** * ** ***

### Meta Domain Verification

Meta may require domain verification for certain advertising features.

Verification values can be entered separately for:

* English (EN)

* French (FR)

#### Obtaining Your Verification Token

1. Open Meta Business Settings.

2. Navigate to **Brand Safety → Domains**.

3. Add and verify your domain.

4. Select **Meta-tag Verification**.

5. Copy the verification value provided by Meta.

*** ** * ** ***

## Reddit Pixel

### Reddit Pixel ID

The Reddit Pixel tracks visitor activity and conversion events originating from Reddit advertising campaigns.

Enter the Reddit Pixel ID associated with your advertising account.

*** ** * ** ***

### Reddit Ads Account ID

The Reddit Ads Account ID identifies the advertising account associated with the configured Reddit Pixel.

Enter the account ID provided within your Reddit Ads Manager account.

*** ** * ** ***

### Reddit Conversions API Access Token

The Reddit Conversions API Access Token allows CrowdChange to send completed transaction events directly to Reddit from the server.

Server-side tracking can improve conversion attribution and reporting reliability.

*** ** * ** ***

## Pinterest Tag

### Pinterest Tag ID

The Pinterest Tag tracks visitor activity and conversion events generated through Pinterest advertising campaigns.

Enter the Tag ID associated with your Pinterest advertising account.

*** ** * ** ***

### Pinterest Ad Account ID

The Pinterest Ad Account ID identifies the advertising account associated with the configured Pinterest Tag.

Enter the account ID provided within Pinterest Business.

*** ** * ** ***

### Pinterest Conversions API Access Token

The Pinterest Conversions API Access Token allows CrowdChange to send completed donation and purchase events directly to Pinterest using secure server-side tracking.

Server-side tracking can improve conversion attribution and reporting accuracy.

*** ** * ** ***

## TikTok Pixel

### TikTok Pixel ID

The TikTok Pixel tracks visitor activity and conversion events generated through TikTok advertising campaigns.

Enter the Pixel ID associated with your TikTok Ads account.

*** ** * ** ***

### TikTok Events API Access Token

The TikTok Events API Access Token allows CrowdChange to send completed transaction events directly to TikTok from the server.

Server-side tracking can improve attribution reliability and help reduce conversion data loss caused by browser privacy restrictions.

*** ** * ** ***

## Best Practices

For the most complete conversion reporting, CrowdChange recommends configuring both:

* Browser-side tracking (Analytics IDs, Pixels, and Tags)

* Server-side tracking (Measurement Protocol and Conversions API integrations)

Using both methods helps advertising and analytics platforms more accurately attribute donations, registrations, ticket purchases, sponsorships, and merchandise sales while reducing data loss caused by browser privacy restrictions.

# How to Pin Featured Fundraisers

You can pin fundraisers to the **Featured**section at the top of your site's homepage so they're always in view!

To do so, just follow these steps:

1. Go to the home page of your CrowdChange site. If you've already created some fundraisers, you'll see them listed as below:

   ![browse.png](../assets/how-to-pin-featured-fundraisers/browse.png)
2. Hover over a fundraiser you would like to pin to the **Featured**section. A star icon is shown in the top right corner. Click it to set / pin the fundraiser as featured.

   ![charityfunrun.png](../assets/how-to-pin-featured-fundraisers/charityfunrun.png)
3. Fundraisers you star / pin will be placed at the top of the page in the **Featured**section

   ![featured.png](../assets/how-to-pin-featured-fundraisers/featured.png)

4. To remove a fundraiser from the **Featured**section, click the star icon again.

   ![remove2.png](../assets/how-to-pin-featured-fundraisers/remove2.png)

Please note that the Featured section is limited to **9**fundraisers.

# Leaderboard & Page Navigation

The **Leaderboard** block is useful not only for inspiring potential donors to contribute, but also for seeing how donors' contributions are showing up. There are 2 sort options - **Top** Donations and **Recent** Donations.  
The Leaderboard block will only be available if '**Show list of donors**' is enabled in fundraiser settings.

On a fundraiser with the **Top Donations List** enabled, as well as **Personal \& Team Fundraising Pages**, the Leaderboard block will look like this:  
![exampleboard.png](../assets/leaderboard-page-navigation/exampleboard.png)

At the bottom of **Top Donations** , click **See All** to be taken to the full **Donations List** shown below.  
Please note that this full list is always sorted by **Most Recent**, regardless of the previous setting.  
![image-20250805-205923.png](../assets/leaderboard-page-navigation/image-20250805-205923.png)

Navigating the **Personal and Team Fundraising Pages** created under your fundraiser is also made easy via their own searchable lists. Click **See All** at the bottom of the **Top Teams** or **Top Pages**lists to access these:

**Teams List:**  
![namesgone.png](../assets/leaderboard-page-navigation/namesgone.png)

**Personal Pages List:**  
![individual.png](../assets/leaderboard-page-navigation/individual.png)

title: Data included in Donations Lists and Amount Raised Bars

- purchase-options

- reporting-and-data
- sponsorship
- ticketing
crm_relevant: true
description: Donations Lists Donations Lists are shown on fundraisers where the ‘Show list of donors’ feature is enabled in fundraiser settings, and they can be either Top …
last_modified: '2023-10-31T14:37:18.732Z'
retrieved: '2026-10-14'
audience: Charity Admins (CrowdChange admin help center space CT)
word_count: 283
---

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/data-included-in-donations-lists-and-amount-raised | Nav: Data included in Donations Lists and Amount Raised Bars | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# Data included in Donations Lists and Amount Raised Bars

## Donations Lists

Donations Lists are shown on fundraisers where the '**Show list of donors** ' feature is enabled in fundraiser settings, and they can be either **Top Donations** or**Recent Donations**, depending on the option selected.

* **Top Donations** lists 10 donations sorted by highest amount. Blank ($0) amounts are sorted by name.

* **Recent Donations** lists 10 donations sorted by the most recent.

Clicking the '**See All** ' button within either list will show **ALL**donations, sorted by most recent.

* These lists always include the donor display name (entered in the '**Show my name as**' field at checkout), and the amount donated unless the donor chose to hide amount. Donors can choose the name they would like to be shown (My name, Anonymous, Family Friend, Supporter, or 'Enter your own name'), and can decide whether to show or hide their donation amount.

* Only Donations, Self-Donations, Sponsorships and Matched amounts are shown in Donations Lists.

* Tickets, apparel, and registrations are **not** included in the amounts shown for each donor.

* If the amount is hidden, or $0 (for example, a ticket purchase only) - only the name is shown with a blank donation amount.

## Amount Raised Bars

Raised amounts include both 'hidden' and 'anonymous' donations and are calculated as follows:

* **On Fundraisers**

  * \[Total Amount without covered or deducted fees\] + \[Matched Amounts\] - \[Refunds\]

  * Note: Total Amount **includes** tickets, apparel, registrations, and sponsorships

* **On Teams**

  * \[Donations to Team\] + \[Donations to Pages\] + \[Self-Donations to Pages\] + \[Matched Amounts\] + \[Sponsorships\] - \[Refunds\]

  * Note: Donations do **NOT** include tickets, apparel, or registrations.

* **On Personal Pages**

  * \[Donations to Page\] + \[Self-Donations to Page\] + \[Matched Amounts\] + \[Sponsorships\] - \[Refunds\]

  * Note: Donations do **NOT** include tickets, apparel, or registrations.

title: How to Reset Your Password

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/how-to-reset-your-password | Nav: How to Reset Your Password | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# How to Reset Your Password

This process must be performed by the user themselves, using the steps below:

1. Go to your CrowdChange site.

2. Click **Login**on the top-right corner of the site.

   ![loginz.png](../assets/how-to-reset-your-password/loginz.png)
3. Within the popup that appears, enter your email and click **Next**.

   ![nextl.png](../assets/how-to-reset-your-password/nextl.png)
4. On the next page, click **Reset password**.

   ![resetit.png](../assets/how-to-reset-your-password/resetit.png)
5. On the next page, click **Next**.

   ![nextk.png](../assets/how-to-reset-your-password/nextk.png)
6. You will be sent an **email**with a link to a Password Reset page.

   ![image-20240902-191436.png](../assets/how-to-reset-your-password/image-20240902-191436.png)
7. Ensure you are still **logged out** of your CrowdChange site, then **click the link** in the email you received.

   ![resetttt.png](../assets/how-to-reset-your-password/resetttt.png)
8. Enter the new password that you would like to use and then click **Save**.

   ![image-20240902-191651.png](../assets/how-to-reset-your-password/image-20240902-191651.png)

Please note that password reset links expire in one hour. If you exceed that time, it will not work, and you will need to request a new link following the same steps above.  
If the user themselves is having trouble doing this, you can complete steps 1 through 5 on their behalf, and have them complete steps 6 and 7 once they have received the reset email.

They must be **logged out** before clicking the password reset link, or they will be directed to their Profile, where they would need to enter the current password as well as the new one.

# How to Cap User Transaction Fees

CrowdChange allows organizations to let their donors cover the transaction fees associated with their donation or purchase, ensuring that 100% of the donation goes to the organization.

This fee is usually a small percentage of the overall donation value, and we find that 93% of the time, given the option, a donor will choose to cover the fees. This structure however can sometimes discourage higher value donations as these fees scale alongside donation value.

CrowdChange is equipped with a **Cap Covered Fees** feature in order to limit the maximum amount that a donor would have to pay. The difference in fees would then be covered by the organization. The **Cap covered fees**function can be applied either by a dollar amount, or a percentage value of the overall donation amount.  
For example, assume that a $100 donation results in $4 in total transaction fees. This amount is for illustration only, as actual fees vary based on factors such as the payment processor, contractual agreement, and card type.

If your site has a covered-fee cap of $2, or 2% of the donation amount, the donor would contribute a maximum of $2 toward those fees. Their total payment would therefore be $102.

The cap does not reduce the transaction fees associated with the payment. Any portion not covered by the donor is absorbed by your organization, and the standard fees outlined in your CrowdChange agreement are deducted from the total transaction amount.

*** ** * ** ***

To use the **Cap Covered Fees**feature, please follow these steps:

1. Go to your CrowdChange site and log in to your administrator account.

2. In the top right-hand corner of your screen, click on **Profile → Admin**.

3. This will bring you to the **General Settings** screen. Toggle on **Cap Covered Fees** and enter a **Maximum Amount** that your donors will be able to cover if they choose to do so.

4. Click **Save**at the bottom of the page to apply your changes.

![image-20260922-144033.png](../assets/how-to-cap-user-transaction-fees/image-20260922-144033.png)
The **Cap covered fees** setting within the **General settings** section of the *Admin dashboard*  
Please note that the **Cap Covered Fees** feature takes effect across your entire CrowdChange site, and will be applied to all fundraisers at once.

# Setting Up Multi-Factor Authentication (2FA)

**Multi-Factor Authentication**(commonly referred to as Two-Factor Authentication or 2FA) is the best way to secure your CrowdChange account against security breaches. This can be set up using the following steps:

1. Go to your CrowdChange site and log in to your account.

2. In the upper right-hand corner of your CrowdChange site, click on **Profile → My Profile**.

3. Scroll down and toggle on **Multi-Factor Authentication**.

![multifactor.png](../assets/setting-up-multi-factor-authentication-2fa/multifactor.png)

There are three options for **Multi-Factor Authentication** - **Email, SMS,** and **Authentication Application**. These options refer to different methods by which a confirmation code will be provided to you in order for you to log in to your account.  
![methods.png](../assets/setting-up-multi-factor-authentication-2fa/methods.png)  
**Authentication Application** is by far the most secure option for **Multi-Factor Authentication** and is, therefore, our recommended choice (for all online applications, not just CrowdChange).

To use this method you will need to install an authentication app on your smartphone (there are some desktop applications as well). Unlike the SMS method, the authentication app method does not rely on receiving a code sent by the platform you want to log into.

When you first configure an authentication app to work with a platform, the app and platform exchange a secret code. This is generally done by using your device's camera to scan a QR code containing the shared secret. Using that secret code, the app then generates a numeric authentication code for you to enter into the platform when required. The authentication apps generate new codes every 30-60 seconds which must be entered before they expire.

**Here is a list of the most popular authentication apps:**

Google Authenticator ([Apple App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/google-authenticator/id388497605), [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.apps.authenticator2&hl=en_CA&gl=US))

Microsoft Authenticator ([Apple App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/microsoft-authenticator/id983156458), [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.azure.authenticator&hl=en_CA&gl=US))

Authy 2-Factor Authentication ([Desktop](https://authy.com/download/), [Apple App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/authy/id494168017), [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.authy.authy))

1Password ([Desktop](https://1password.com/downloads/), [Apple App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/1password-password-manager/id568903335), [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.agilebits.onepassword))

LastPass ([Desktop/Browser](https://lastpass.com/misc_download2.php), [Apple App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/lastpass-for-premium-customers/id324613447?ign-mpt=uo%3D4), [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.lastpass.lpandroid))

# Stripe Banking Overview

**Stripe** is one of the payment processors that CrowdChange is partnered with.  
CrowdChange works with different payment processors depending on the needs of your organization. If you have any questions about which payment processor is right for your organization, don't hesitate to reach out to your Partner Success Representative to discuss your options.

*** ** * ** ***

**Stripe Security**

Stripe is **Level 1 PCI Compliant** , which is the most stringent level of security available in the payment processing industry. For context, Stripe has never had a breach of data in the history of their company. They are used by UnderArmour, Unicef, Habitat for Humanity, Lyft, and many more (a full list of charitable clients, as well as non-charitable clients, can be found here: <https://stripe.com/customers#nonprofits> ).

While CrowdChange itself is also PCI Compliant, all sensitive credit card information is stored with Stripe through tokenization, thus no sensitive credit card information is stored on the CrowdChange platform. The CRA (Canadian Revenue Agency) requires Stripe to collect account owner information to help combat tax fraud, stop donations coming from flagged organizations, and other security concerns. Please note that this is not something that CrowdChange or Stripe mandate but rather something that is required by government regulators. Take a look at some Stripe documentation, as well as Canadian Government *Know your Customer* (KYC) requirements below:

* [Stripe's KYC acknowledgement and required fields depending on your location](https://support.stripe.com/questions/know-your-customer)

* [Minimum requirements for Canadian Clients](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/required-verification-information)

* [Government requirements to adhere to KYC rules](http://www.fintrac-canafe.gc.ca/guidance-directives/client-clientele/Guide11/11-eng.asp)

* CrowdChange uses Stripe's connect accounts to make it easy for charitable partners to collect funds. CrowdChange qualifies as an *Account-Based Business Relationship* and is therefore required to adhere to KYC rules. [More information on CRA requirements can be found here.](http://www.fintrac-canafe.gc.ca/guidance-directives/client-clientele/Guide11/11-eng.asp)

Stripe has the ability to put fundraisers on hold until banking information has been entered to your CrowdChange site to ensure that they are following all Canadian rules and regulations (CrowdChange is based in Canada). In order to ensure your campaign runs uninterrupted, we recommend entering all required banking fields as soon as possible.

*** ** * ** ***

## **Setting Up Stripe Banking**

**Scenario 1 - Fundraiser-Level Banking**

If your organization is using Stripe as their payment processor, and their CrowdChange site is set up for Users Manage Banking, banking can be set up by following these steps at the fundraiser level:

1. Go to your fundraiser and log in to your CrowdChange account.

2. Click **Manage Fundraiser** in the top right, then **Banking → My Banking Settings**.

3. Fill out the required fields with your organization's banking information.

**Scenario 2 - Universal/Global Banking**

If your CrowdChange site uses **Universal/Global** Banking (all fundraisers on the site use the same bank account), then this can only be entered at the site-wide level on the **Admin** page.

1. Go to your CrowdChange site and **Log In** with your admin credentials.

2. Click on **Profile** then **Admin**in the upper-right hand corner of your window.

3. Click **Banking settings** on the left sidebar, then **Stripe**.

4. Enter your organization's banking and representative information.

   *Example below:*

   ![Capture d’écran 2024-12-27 à 18.17.50.png](../assets/stripe-banking-overview/Capture_d_e_cran_2024-12-27_a__18.17.50.png)

Please note that all banking information must be an**exact match**to what has been provided by your bank in order for Stripe to approve your fundraiser for payments.

*** ** * ** ***

### **Payouts - Manual or Automatic**

Admins now have the ability to schedule their payouts **manually**- however, in this case, you will no longer be able to see which transactions are included in a payout.

Alternatively, you can select **automatic**, and Stripe will process all donations on a rolling basis, meaning that a donation is processed on the schedule set (daily/weekly/monthly), after it is received by your fundraiser. After a donation is processed it will be deposited directly into your bank account - depending on the payout schedule configured.

To set adjust your payout schedule, follow the steps below:

1. Go to your CrowdChange site and **Log In** with your admin credentials.

2. Click on **Profile** then **Admin**in the upper-right hand corner of your window.

3. Click **Banking settings** on the left sidebar, then **Stripe**.

4. Under **Balance \& Payout Settings** , click **See details**.

   ![see details.png](../assets/stripe-banking-overview/see_details.png)
5. Within the sidebar that appears, click **Update**under the 'On the way to your bank' section.

   ![update.png](../assets/stripe-banking-overview/update.png)
6. If desired, select **Manual** under **Schedule** , and click **Save**at the bottom of the page.

   ![manualsave.png](../assets/stripe-banking-overview/manualsave.png)
7. Under **Balance \& Payout Settings** , click **Pay out.**

   ![payout.png](../assets/stripe-banking-overview/payout.png)
8. You will then be able to manually trigger a payout of your desired amount.

   ![image-20250215-191343.png](../assets/stripe-banking-overview/image-20250215-191343.png)

*** ** * ** ***

**Looking for Support?**

Having issues with your banking setup? CrowdChange Support would be happy to investigate for you! Simply click the blue **Help**button in the bottom right corner of this page, fill out the details, and our support team will get back to you as soon as possible!

# Paysafe Banking Overview

**Paysafe**is one of the payment processors that CrowdChange is partnered with.  
CrowdChange works with different payment processors depending on the needs of your organization. If you have any questions about which payment processor is right for your organization, don't hesitate to reach out to your Partner Success Representative to discuss your options.

*** ** * ** ***

**Paysafe Security**

Paysafe is **Level 1 PCI Compliant**, which is the most stringent level of security available in the payment processing industry. Paysafe is audited annually and has maintained its PCI DSS for over 10 years.

From Paysafe's website:
> Paysafe's payment gateway processes millions of transactions per day globally, and we understand the importance of security and our role in helping our customers protect sensitive data.

The CRA (Canadian Revenue Agency) requires Paysafe to collect account owner information to help combat tax fraud, stop donations coming from flagged organizations, and other security concerns. Please note that this is not something that CrowdChange or Paysafe mandate but rather something that is required by government regulators.

*** ** * ** ***

**Setting Up Paysafe Banking**

All Paysafe banking settings are completed with Paysafe directly.  
The sign-up link that your Partner Success Representative has provided is unique to your organization and will have any negotiated rates associated with it. **Do not attempt to sign up with Paysafe using any link other than what has been provided to you.**

Once your organization has completed the sign-up process with Paysafe, all that is required on your CrowdChange site is to provide the Paysafe Account ID that is issued to your account. This can be done by accessing the **Banking** page within the **Admin** menu. Please see the image below:  
![bankingpaysafe (1).png](../assets/paysafe-banking-overview/bankingpaysafe__1).png?cb=439885ca62ea1b3b146db1ccdb1ad14e)  
Once you have entered your Paysafe Account ID on the Banking page, your account information will populate in the box to the right of this information. **Please confirm your account details prior to launching any fundraisers in order to ensure that your account is linked correctly.**

*** ** * ** ***

**Payouts**

**Payout Reports** are not available within your CrowdChange admin reporting - this information will live within your Paysafe dashboard.

*** ** * ** ***

**Issues with your banking setup?**

CrowdChange Support would be happy to investigate for you! Simply click the blue **Help**button in the bottom right corner of this page, fill out the details, and our support team will get back to you as soon as possible!  
**Issues with your Paysafe account?**

Contact Paysafe support directly.

**Contact information:**

Customer service and technical support phone number: 1(888)709-8753

Partner Phone number: 1(800)361-4983

[partnersupport@paysafe.com](mailto:partnersupport@paysafe.com): Non-technical issues

[partnertechsupport@paysafe.com](mailto:partnertechsupport@paysafe.com): Technical issues

For **urgent** support, please contact [support@crowdchange.co](mailto:support@crowdchange.co) in order for our team to escalate any issues (inability to accept payments etc.)

# Failed Transaction

Failed transactions can be the result of many factors including, but not limited to, the following:

* **Interrupted internet service**

  * Confirm your internet connection is stable and refresh the page, then retry your transaction.

* **Incorrect Billing Address**

  * Please make sure that your billing address is an exact match to the billing information associated with your Credit Card or else the payment will not be able to process.

* **Time-out**

  * Time-outs are common and usually caused by the following:

    * Page being left open for an extended period of time causing the token to expire.

    * Switching apps while filling out the form / billing info.

* **Internet browser being used**

  * Try a different web browser, or an incognito / private tab. We recommend Google Chrome. If you are still having trouble, turn off all plugins such as Adblock, refresh the page and try again.

* **Mistake in the payment information entered**

  * Double and triple-check that all payment information is correct.

Re-attempt your transaction. If you are still unable to process your transaction please contact us by clicking the blue **Help**button in the bottom right corner of this page.

## CSRF Token Mismatch

This is a common error message which can be caused by the following:

1. **Browser plugins** such as Adblock

2. Using **Incognito / Private browsing modes**

3. **Time-outs** (page being open for an extended period of time causing the token to expire) - Time-outs can also be caused on some devices by switching apps while filling out the form / billing info.

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/salesforce-integration-with-crowdchange | Nav: Salesforce Integration with CrowdChange | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# Salesforce Integration with CrowdChange

## **How does CrowdChange integrate with Salesforce?**

CrowdChange is equipped with Salesforce integration through Connected Apps. A Connected App is a framework which enables an external application to integrate with Salesforce using APIs and standard protocols, such as SAML, OAuth, and OpenID Connect. Connected Apps use these protocols to authenticate, authorize, and provide single sign-on (SSO) for external apps. The external apps that are integrated with Salesforce can run on the customer success platform, other platforms, devices, or SaaS subscriptions.

For example, when you log in to your Salesforce mobile app and see your data from your Salesforce org, you're using a Connected App.  
Using Salesforce but not set up for integration? Speak to your Partner Success Representative to discuss your options. CrowdChange sites are not set up for Salesforce Integration by default.

## **How can I enable Salesforce integration on my CrowdChange site?**

In order to enable Salesforce integration, follow these steps:

1. Go to your CrowdChange site and log in to your account. Please note that administrator access is required to enable Salesforce integration.

2. In the upper right-hand corner of your screen, click **Profile** , then **Admin** . In the left-hand sidebar, click **Integrations** , then **Salesforce Integration**.

3. On the screen below, input your **Salesforce custom domain** into the box pictured below, then click **Connect to Salesforce**. This will then open a new tab that will redirect you to Salesforce - please allow CrowdChange access in order to initialize this connection.

![image-20240724-152058.png](../assets/salesforce-integration-with-crowdchange/image-20240724-152058.png)  
![image-20240724-152213.png](../assets/salesforce-integration-with-crowdchange/image-20240724-152213.png)  
Please note that all entries made in Salesforce by CrowdChange will be logged under the email address of the user who completes this integration process - for example, if you log in to your Salesforce account using the email address [kevin@crowdchange.co](mailto:kevin@crowdchange.co), all entries that CrowdChange creates in Salesforce will be entered under the [kevin@crowdchange.co](mailto:kevin@crowdchange.co) email address.

We recommend creating a CrowdChange specific account to complete this integration in order to differentiate CrowdChange entries from any other entries made under your existing Salesforce account. This will allow you to better track data.

**Salesforce Integration Settings**

Once your Salesforce Integration is complete, there are a few options that will display.

* **Enable Integration**

  * If this option is toggled on, transactions and campaigns will be created in Salesforce (Fundraisers have their options to enable data going through to Salesforce).

* **Opportunity Stage**

  * This allows you to select Opportunity Stage for all new donations (Opportunities) when transactions are added in Salesforce.

![image-20240724-152828.png](../assets/salesforce-integration-with-crowdchange/image-20240724-152828.png)

## Mapping

**Default Fields**

With no adjustments, data from CrowdChange will be imported into Salesforce with the following mapping applied:

*Account*  

| **Salesforce Field** |       **CrowdChange Field**       |
|----------------------|-----------------------------------|
| Name                 | user.name                         |
| Description          | CrowdChange Account ID: {user_id} |
| Type                 | Other                             |
| BillingStreet        | billing.address                   |
| BillingCity          | billing.city                      |
| BillingState         | billing.state                     |
| BillingPostalCode    | billing.zip                       |
| BillingCountry       | billing.country                   |

*Contact*  

| **Salesforce Field** | **CrowdChange Field** |
|----------------------|-----------------------|
| FirstName            | user.first_name       |
| LastName             | user.last_name        |
| Email                | user.email            |
| MailingStreet        | billing.address       |
| MailingCity          | billing.city          |
| MailingState         | billing.state         |
| MailingPostalCode    | billing.zip           |
| MailingCountry       | billing.country       |
| LeadSource           | CrowdChange           |

*Opportunity*  

| **Salesforce Field** |          **CrowdChange Field**           |
|----------------------|------------------------------------------|
| Name                 | Donation to {fundraiser.name}            |
| Amount               | transaction.amount                       |
| CloseDate            | transaction.date                         |
| StageName            | \[Stage\]                                |
| CampaignId           | \[Campaign ID\]                          |
| Type                 | Donation                                 |
| Description          | Donation made through \[Fundraiser URL\] |

*Payment*  

|  **Salesforce Field**  | **CrowdChange Field**  |
|------------------------|------------------------|
| Payment Amount         | transaction.amount     |
| Payment Date           | transaction.date       |
| Check Reference Number | transaction.id         |
| Payment Method         | transaction.pay_method |
| Paid                   | true                   |
| Written Off            | false                  |

**Fundraiser Settings**

If SalesForce integration is enabled, you will see a new section when creating or updating fundraisers.  
![image-20240724-155019.png](../assets/salesforce-integration-with-crowdchange/image-20240724-155019.png)

If the **Import to Salesforce** option is toggled on, all transactions for this fundraiser will be added to Salesforce. By default, the name of your fundraiser will be the name of the campaign created in Salesforce, but this can be changed using the text box underneath **Campaign** .

**Data Flow**

If Salesforce integration is enabled, and **Import to Salesforce** is enabled at the fundraiser level, all online transactions (NOT offline donations) will be imported into Salesforce.

* When a transaction is made, we will attempt to locate an existing Contact by email. If there is no match, we will try to match to existing contact by First Name + Last Name + Postal Code.

  If there is still no match, a new Contact will be created in Salesforce from the User information that we have on file in CrowdChange.

* Since Opportunities are assigned to Accounts, not Contacts - CrowdChange will only look for contacts with an Account ID associated with them. If an existing Contact is found without an Account ID, it will not be used.

* In the case where a Contact is not found with an Account ID, we will try to locate the Account that was previously created by CrowdChange. If no account is found, we will create a new account and try to create a new Contact for that account.

![image-20211026-194550.png](../assets/salesforce-integration-with-crowdchange/image-20211026-194550.png)

* Donation data will create a New Opportunity in Salesforce. If the Non-Profit Success Package (NPSP) is installed, there will be additional payment data created (payment method, currency, etc).

![image-20211026-194747.png](../assets/salesforce-integration-with-crowdchange/image-20211026-194747.png)  
![image-20211026-194801.png](../assets/salesforce-integration-with-crowdchange/image-20211026-194801.png)

* Opportunity will be linked to Campaign if the Campaign field was used when setting up your Fundraiser.

Please note that**Offline Donations** entered in CrowdChange do not get exported to Salesforce.

================================================================================

# Integrating CrowdChange with Raiser's Edge and Raiser's Edge NXT

**Importacular** by Zeidman Development is your import tool for bringing all CrowdChange information into Blackbaud Raiser's Edge and Raiser's Edge NXT. See the video below for a brief introduction to Importacular:

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2gSMEB9gJXk>  
CrowdChange charges a one-time fee to build a custom API in order to connect your CrowdChange site to Importacular. This fee also covers the development costs of maintaining this connection over the life cycle of the CrowdChange platform.

For details, please contact your Partner Success Manager to discuss.

## **Installing Importacular**

Importacular is a free plug-in for Raiser's Edge and Raiser's Edge NXT. It is available for both Blackbaud-hosted and self-hosted accounts.

If your Raiser's Edge or Raiser's Edge NXT account is hosted by Blackbaud, Importacular is available as a default plug-in. If you do not see Importacular in your plug-ins section, contact [Zeidman Development](https://www.zeidman.info/contact).

If you are self-hosted, please [register for a **ZeidZone** account](https://www.zeidman.info/registration/) to download the plug-in.

### **Using Importacular**

Once the Importacular plug-in is installed, take a look at our [CrowdChange Import Demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rSV5PSzdTu4) video for further information on how to integrate your CrowdChange site with Raiser's Edge and Raiser's Edge NXT.  
Please note that you will need to determine the mapping of all fields within Importacular.

See the below list of all fields available to map into Raiser's Edge and Raiser's Edge NXT from CrowdChange using Importacular.

[Importacular - CrowdChange Data Fields.pdf](https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/__attachments/a_a618160dacc4249cba6992875487c27356f366aa052a2dde2405b45024487234/Importacular%2520-%2520CrowdChange%2520Data%2520Fields.pdf?cb=b833e367496b94ef884b1a293a9b6763)

Here are is some more information you may find useful:

* [Tribute/In-Memory Import](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WbOSwxQ8VbI&feature=emb_title) / See article [here](https://www.zeidman.info/docs/importacular-user-guide-3/import-to-honor-memorial-and-tribute/) as well.

* [Importing Constituent Data](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cxHZb0hXwI8&feature=emb_title)

* [Importing Addresses with Importacular](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4ciDMeeljbU&feature=emb_title)

* [Importing Gifts into Raiser's Edge and Raiser's Edge NXT](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oXNFWXMFf50&feature=emb_title)

* [Creating a mapping template](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pl7IzJcV74I&feature=emb_title)

Please note that data flow from CrowdChange to Raiser's Edge and Raiser's Edge NXT through Importacular is **not**automatic. You must manually initiate the upload in order to see results in Raiser's Edge and Raiser's Edge NXT.

### **Looking for support?**

Your main support portal for the Importacular plug-in will be the [Zeidman Development **Importacular User's Guide**](https://www.zeidman.info/docs/importacular-user-guide-3/overview/). This is a comprehensive online knowledgebase detailing how you can best connect your CrowdChange site with Importacular. This guide contains installation instructions and explains the complete functionality of the Importacular plug-in.

Many troubleshooting solutions are available via a quick search in the [**Zeidman Development Support Page**](https://zeiddev.freshdesk.com/support/solutions/folders/270245), which outlines issues that users have raised to Zeidman Development.

All additional support from Zeidman Development is available at a cost.

**Zeidman Development does not offer real-time support, even to those who do opt-in to their paid support option.**

# DonorPerfect Integration with CrowdChange

CrowdChange is able to connect with your organization's DonorPerfect account, and automatically upload relevant data to DonorPerfect instantly on a transaction-by-transaction basis.  
Is your organization using DonorPerfect, but has not been set up for integration with CrowdChange? For a one-time fee, we can connect your site to DonorPerfect. This cost goes towards the creation and maintenance of the connection between CrowdChange and DonorPerfect.

For details, feel free to contact your Partner Success Manager!

## **What do you need from DonorPerfect?**

In order for you to connect your CrowdChange site to DonorPerfect, you need to request an API key (which is a long series of letters, numbers, and special characters) from them directly. This is then generated in your DonorPerfect account. Reach out to your contact at DonorPerfect to ask for an API key to connect to your CrowdChange account, and they can set this up for you.

### **Setting the connection up on your CrowdChange site**

Once you have secured the API key from DonorPerfect, this needs to be entered into your CrowdChange site. Please follow these steps to do this:

1. Go to your CrowdChange site and log in to your account.

2. In the upper right-hand corner of your screen, click **Profile → Admin.**

3. In the sidebar of the **Admin** dashboard, click **Integrations** → **DonorPerfect Integration**.

4. Toggle on **Enable Integration** and paste the API key into the text box. Be sure to click **Save** once these steps are completed.

![dp2.png](../assets/donorperfect-integration-with-crowdchange/dp2.png)  
Your API key must match **exactly**with what has been provided to you by DonorPerfect. Please use the copy and paste function to input your API key in order to avoid errors.

### **Applying the connection to your campaigns**

Once your site has DonorPerfect Integration enabled, and you have entered your API Key, when creating or editing fundraisers you will now have an option called **Import to DonorPerfect** under the **Advanced Features** section of the **Additional Settings**page.  
![DP.png](../assets/donorperfect-integration-with-crowdchange/DP.png)

When creating a fundraiser you will have the option to enter in the following codes:

* Campaign Code

* General Ledger Code

* Appeal (Solicitation) Code

If any of these codes are set, there will be a check if it already exists in DonorPerfect when a transaction is imported. If a code already exists, it will be used to import the transaction with that value. If it does not exist, a new code will be created in DonorPerfect that will have Fundraiser's Name as `DESCRIPTION`, and Campaign Code as `CODE`.  
![image-20211123-170044.png](../assets/donorperfect-integration-with-crowdchange/image-20211123-170044.png)

This can be updated later by clicking "Manage Codes" in DonorPerfect:  
![image-20211123-170120.png](../assets/donorperfect-integration-with-crowdchange/image-20211123-170120.png)

If `Codes` are **not set**, they will be set to empty field in the DonorPerfect system.

### **Data Passed to DonorPerfect**

#### Donor

Donor is only created when we cannot find a match to an existing donor in DonorPerfect. CrowdChange will initially look for donors by matching their email address to your DonorPerfect account, then by first name, last name, city, and ZIP/Postal Code. If all fail, then a new donor will be created with the following fields:

* Salutation (Title)

* First Name

* Last Name

* Address (street, city, state, zip, country)

* Email

* No Mail (subscription status)

* Address Type = HOME

* Donor Type = Individual

* Created By = CrowdChange Inc.

#### Gift

Gift is a transaction on your CrowdChange site. Gifts are created with the following fields:

* Donor (links to either existing or newly created donor)

* Amount (full transaction amount, including fees)

* Currency

* Campaign (if was set in Fundraiser settings)

* General Ledger (if was set in Fundraiser settings)

* Appeal Code (if was set in Fundraiser settings)

* Receipt = Yes if tax receipt was issued, otherwise No

* Tax Receipt Number

* Tax Receipt Status

* Tax Receipt Date

* Pledge Payment = No

* Split Payment = No

* Do Not Calculate = No

* Batch Number = 0

* Reference Number = Transaction ID in CrowdChange

* Receipt Delivery = Email

* Record Type = Gift

### **Refunds**

When a refund or dispute happens, three things occur in DonorPerfect:

1. **Original Gift is modified**

   * Record Type = A (Adjustment)

   * Modified By = CrowdChange Inc.

   * Modified Date

2. **New Adjustment Gift is created**

   * Amount = Negative amount of original transaction (\[amount\] x -1)

   * Record Type = H

   * Gift Date = refund date

3. **New Resulting Gift is created**

   * Amount = 0

   * Record Type = C

   * Gift Date = refund date

### **Looking for Support?**

You can always reach out to CrowdChange Support at [support@crowdchange.co](mailto:support@crowdchange.co) with any technical requests. Or simply click the blue **Help**button at the bottom right of this page!

================================================================================
