# How to Add Custom Fields to the Start a Fundraiser Process

Need to collect additional information from fundraiser creators on your site?

You have the ability to add custom fields to the Start a Fundraiser process, similar to how [Custom Questions](how-to-use-custom-questions.md) work on the checkout page. You can add as many as you need!  
Please note that this feature is **NOT**enabled by default and you will need to reach out to your Partner Success Representative directly to have it enabled for your site(s).

Some common use cases for this feature are for example - if you need to:

* Collect phone numbers or other contact information from fundraiser creators

* Require waivers to be signed (or Terms of Use be agreed to) pre-launch

* Ask Survey type questions to gather information from fundraiser creators

These fields can be set up from **Profile \> Admin \> Fundraisers Settings \> Custom Fields**and show up when creating or editing fundraisers.

All responses can be found later in the[**Admin Fundraisers Report**](how-to-access-the-fundraisers-report.md).

## Detailed Steps

To get started and add your first custom field, follow these steps:

1. Log in to a CrowdChange account with admin permissions.

2. Click **Profile → Admin**in the upper right-hand corner of your CrowdChange site.

3. Click **Fundraisers Settings → Custom Fields**

4. On the **Custom Fields** page, you can click **Add Question** to create a question or field, which will be shown during the creation process of a fundraiser.

5. Fill out the **Question** and **Content** fields (if applicable), then select a **Type** (Text Box *- contains sub-types* , Multi-Line Text, Checkboxes, Dropdown or Waiver), and whether the question will be **Required**or not. Here are a few example questions:

   ![image-20240930-181431.png](../assets/how-to-add-custom-fields-to-the-start-a-fundraiser/image-20240930-181431.png)

   You can return to this page at any time to **Edit** , **Remove** , or **Add**custom questions / fields.

If you require the ability to set**Custom ID's** for each question, reach out to your Partner Success Representative for this feature to be enabled on your site.

## Fundraiser Creator's View

Once you have added your custom questions / fields, going forward, all fundraiser creators on your CrowdChange site will see the created questions in the final section of the Start a Fundraiser process, called Additional Questions, as shown below:  
![required.png](../assets/how-to-add-custom-fields-to-the-start-a-fundraiser/required.png)

They will not be able to create their fundraiser until any required questions are answered.  
Remember that you can access all answers to these custom fields in the [**Admin Fundraisers Report**](how-to-access-the-fundraisers-report.md).

# Custom Questions for Teams & Personal Pages

Need to gather specific information from Team Captains or Personal Page creators? You're bound to love our custom questions feature for Teams \& Personal Pages!

Using it, you can create questions (including conditional questions), which are asked when someone is creating a team or personal page, via our simplified peer-to-peer, or multi-registration workflows.  
Please note that this feature is **NOT**enabled by default.

Reach out to your Partner Success Representative today to explore how this functionality could benefit your campaign!

See instructions below for how to set up Team and Personal Page Questions:
Setting up Team Questions  

## Setting up Team Questions

1. On a fundraiser where Team Fundraising Pages are enabled, click**Manage Fundraiser** , then**Peer to Peer settings** on the left sidebar.

2. Click **Team Fundraising Pages** and scroll down to **Custom Questions**.

3. Click **Add Question** to create a custom team question.

   ![add qu.png](../assets/custom-questions-for-teams-personal-pages/add_qu.png)
4. Select your question **Type** (Text, Checkboxes, Dropdown, Waiver or Multi-line text), sub-type (if applicable), fill out the details of your question, and click **Save** when finished.

   ![SAVEZZZZ.png](../assets/custom-questions-for-teams-personal-pages/SAVEZZZZ.png)
5. Add in as many questions as needed (optional, conditional or required), ensuring to **Save**.

6. When creating a new team, creators/captains will be asked the custom questions.

   1. During the normal "Start a Team" process:

      ![phonenum.png](/__attachments/a_9e28b44a4c97f06278463cd335c075acb21fb636e8a4e6ad70f7898723362895/phonenum.png?cb=d9d347a56308224e5d8ee6ef4ec67bdf)
   2. During the multi-registration team creation process:

      ![phonenumber.png](/__attachments/a_209fb932903856f213694c31095b9316f55c38b4126a07b918962e84a6fa03cc/phonenumber.png?cb=6acb6995920c1761b38d7350586d9323)
Setting up Personal Page Questions  

## Setting up Personal Page Questions

1. On a fundraiser where Personal Fundraising Pages are enabled, click**Manage Fundraiser** , then**Peer to Peer settings** on the left sidebar.

2. Click **Personal Fundraising Pages** and scroll down to **Custom Questions**.

3. Click **Add Question** to create a custom personal page question.

   ![addqu2.png](../assets/custom-questions-for-teams-personal-pages/addqu2.png)
4. Select your question **Type** (Text, Checkboxes, Dropdown, Waiver or Multi-line text), sub-type (if applicable), fill out the details of your question, and click **Save** when finished.

   ![SAVEZZZZ.png](../assets/custom-questions-for-teams-personal-pages/SAVEZZZZ.png)
5. Add in as many questions as needed (optional, conditional or required), ensuring to **Save**.

6. When creating a new personal page, creators will be asked the custom questions during the normal (non multi-reg) "Start a Fundraising Page" process:

   ![phonenum4.png](../assets/custom-questions-for-teams-personal-pages/phonenum4.png)

## **Conditional Questions**

You can also ask **Conditional Questions** within your Team and Personal Page Custom Questions.

These are questions which will only show up if a certain condition is met relating to a previous question.

For example, a question like '*What is your team's registration number?* ' could appear after the response '*Yes* ' is given for '*Is your team registered with X organization?*'.

To set this up, you will create both questions you would like your donors to answer (following the instructions above) - the Parent question, and the Child question.

The Parent question must be either a **Single Selection** or **Multiple Choice** question - it cannot be a **Text** or **Waiver**question. See example parent question below:  
![parent1.png](../assets/custom-questions-for-teams-personal-pages/parent1.png)

Now you can create the Child question and set it to appear only if a specific answer is given to the Parent question. To do so, once you've created it, toggle on **Set Conditions**.

Here you can select the (Parent) question which the Child question should be linked to, and determine what answers should cause the Child question to appear. See example below:  
![child1.png](../assets/custom-questions-for-teams-personal-pages/child1.png)

Be sure to click **Save** in the bottom right when you are finished.

## Additional Information

The answers to these questions will be visible in the Admin **Teams Report** and **Personal Pages Report**.

Additionally, the answers to these questions are editable from the **Manage my Team** / **Manage my Page** → **Team Settings / Page Settings** menus at any time.

If using **Blueprints**, you will have the ability to set these questions at the blueprint level and apply to all connected fundraisers.  
If you require the ability to set**Custom ID's** for each question, reach out to your Partner Success Representative for this feature to be enabled on your site.

# Minimum Fundraising Commitment tied to Registration

CrowdChange offers the ability for fundraiser hosts to set a Minimum Fundraising Goal \& Commitment amount tied to Registrations - this means that participants who register with personal fundraising pages commit to raising their goal amount (no less than the minimum set by the fundraiser host), and if this fundraising commitment is not met, they are charged the shortfall.

## **How this feature works**

This feature allows you to set a minimum fundraising goal for a registration tier.

It also allows you to collect Credit Card information to later charge your participants the value of any shortfall in their fundraising (at the end of the campaign).

The ability to track fundraising progress and charge registrants for their shortfall is available in the accompanying Admin **Registration Commitment Report**.

## **How to enable it**

**Please Note** : This feature is **NOT**enabled by default - Reach out to your Partner Success Representative today to discuss how it can benefit your campaign!

Once the feature has been enabled on your site, when setting up a fundraiser, toggle on **Registrations require min. amount commitment** within the **Registration features** section:  
![mincommitment.png](../assets/minimum-fundraising-commitment-tied-to-registratio/mincommitment.png)

Scroll down and click **Create Fundraiser** , then go to your fundraiser and click **Manage Fundraiser → Purchase Options → Registration**to create a registration tier.

If an existing registration tier had already been purchased, you would not be able to add this feature (since registrants were not required to use a minimum goal, and did not see any text regarding minimum commitments when they registered).

Create a new registration tier, and enter your minimum commitment amount in the **Min. Goal Amount** field.  
![1000.png](../assets/minimum-fundraising-commitment-tied-to-registratio/1000.png)

## **How this looks for participants**

Once a minimum goal amount has been set for a registration tier, it will be applied at registration in the Personal Fundraising Page section. If the user enters a number smaller than the minimum amount, they will be prompted to increase it and will not be able to proceed without doing so.

Registrants will now, based on the registration tier they select, be required to input a goal that meets the minimum amount set by the fundraiser host when the registration tier was created.  
![goalcommit.png](../assets/minimum-fundraising-commitment-tied-to-registratio/goalcommit.png)

On the checkout page, there will be another message explaining that the credit card entered will be charged any shortfall in funds raised (if the fundraising goal is not reached). With these settings applied, even users who register for free (via a free registration tier or using a promo code) will still need to input a credit card, allowing you to charge the card later for any fundraising shortfall.  
![notice.png](../assets/minimum-fundraising-commitment-tied-to-registratio/notice.png)

## **Admin Registration Commitment Report**

Reporting capability to track the progress of these financial commitments and who will be charged what amount is available within the Admin **Registration Commitment Report**.

To access this report, simply follow the steps below:

1. From anywhere on your CrowdChange site, click **Profile** in the top right corner, then **Admin**.

2. On the left sidebar, click**Reports \> Registration Commitment Report**.

3. Here you can track fundraising progress and charge registrants for any shortfall.

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/how-to-set-up-custom-fees | Nav: How to Set Up Custom Fees | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# How to Set Up Custom Fees

CrowdChange offers the capability to add **custom fees**per fundraiser / event if necessary.

For example, if you need to add a separate 'Shipping Cost' to each apparel purchase on your fundraiser.

Custom fees can be a specific dollar amount or a percentage, and may be tax-deductible or not.  
**Please note:** this feature is **NOT**available by default and must be enabled by CrowdChange staff.

* Custom fee amounts can be refunded as part of a Partial Refund from the Admin Donations Report.

* Custom fees can also be set per Blueprint, allowing you to copy set fees to connected fundraisers.

* Promo Codes can be applied to custom fees in the same way they are applied to purchase options.

*** ** * ** ***

## Enabling Custom Fees on a Fundraiser

1. **Log In**and navigate to your fundraiser.

2. Click **Manage Fundraiser**in the top-right section of the page.

   ![image-20250812-144706.png](../assets/how-to-set-up-custom-fees/image-20250812-144706.png)

3. Click**Purchase Options** on the left sidebar, then**Custom Fees**.

   ![image-20250812-145149.png](../assets/how-to-set-up-custom-fees/image-20250812-145149.png)

4. Enable **Custom Fees** and click **Save**.

   ![image-20250812-145655.png](../assets/how-to-set-up-custom-fees/image-20250812-145655.png)

## Adding/Creating a Custom Fee

1. **Log In**and navigate to your fundraiser.

2. Click **Manage Fundraiser**in the top-right section of the page.

   ![image-20250812-144706.png](../assets/how-to-set-up-custom-fees/image-20250812-144706.png)
3. Click**Purchase Options** on the left sidebar, then**Custom Fees**.

   ![image-20250812-145149.png](../assets/how-to-set-up-custom-fees/image-20250812-145149.png)
4. Click **Add Fee**.

   ![image-20250812-145803.png](../assets/how-to-set-up-custom-fees/image-20250812-145803.png)

5. Name your custom fee and enter a dollar or percentage amount.

6. Select the purchase option(s) this fee should apply to.

7. Choose whether the fee is tax deductible or not.

   ![image-20250812-150022.png](../assets/how-to-set-up-custom-fees/image-20250812-150022.png)

8. Click **Save** to complete.

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/personal-page-privacy-feature | Nav: Personal Page Privacy Feature | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# Personal Page Privacy Feature

When enabled, the Personal Page Privacy feature makes all personal pages across your CrowdChange site private. This means that they can not be seen or accessed by the general public - only via a direct link to the page. When users create Personal Pages, they receive an email which contains the direct link to their page. They can then share this unique link to anyone they would like to have access to donate to their page.  
This feature is **NOT**enabled by default and can only be enabled by a CrowdChange Admin.

## This feature also means the following (by default):

* Donors cannot search for personal pages or view the list.

* Donors cannot donate through a participant without a direct link to their personal page.

* Donors cannot see personal pages within teams.

* Personal Page owners are unable to see other personal pages while logged in.

* Team owners can only see transactions made to the team, not to team members.

* Fundraiser Hosts can only see that a donation was made to the fundraiser or to a team. If a donation was made through a personal page, the host is unable to see which page the donation came through.

If you'd still like to allow donors to search for personal pages and view the list, simply enable the '**Allow to search for personal pages** ' toggle in **Admin → General Settings**.  
Site Admins can access private personal pages (without a direct link) via **Admin \> Reports \> Personal Pages Report**.

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/parent-child-sub-site-relationship | Nav: Parent - Child / Sub-Site Relationship | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# Parent - Child / Sub-Site Relationship

CrowdChange is equipped with some very useful functionality whereby organizations can set up child sites, also known as sub-sites, under / within a parent site.

For our Charity partners this can be very practical for uses cases such as the following:

* Segmenting individual giving programs

* Specific campaigns which need to be segmented / set apart (for marketing purposes)

* Large-scale multi-region campaigns where you want a dedicated site, with a dedicated fundraiser for each region

**IMPORTANT TO NOTE:**  
* A Parent site can have multiple Child Sites.

* A Child site can only be attached to one Parent site.

* Partners can create as many child sites as they want at no additional cost.

## Managing Child Site Features

Most features of a child site are managed from the child site itself and can be configured independently of Parent sites. There are however, the following exceptions, which are governed by the Parent site:  

|     **Feature**      |                                                              **Description**                                                              |
|----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Banking              | Banking in most cases is managed from the Parent site, however, there are different banking settings that can be applied to a child site. |
| Organizations        | Organizations are managed from the Parent site, and cannot be changed, deleted, or added on child sites.                                  |
| Tax Receipt Settings | Tax Receipt settings are managed from the Parent site and pushed to child.                                                                |
| In Support Of values | "In support of" values are managed from the Parent site, and cannot be changed, deleted, or added from child sites.                       |

The above settings are pushed down to child sites regardless of their settings / features.

### Banking

We offer several different banking configurations and integration with different payment processors, depending on the needs of the client. Banking can also be different for the Parent site than the child site if desired.

Our 3 most common configurations for child site banking are:

* **Central / Global Banking** - Banking is set up on Parent site and automatically pushed to child sites. This can be used with any payment processor.

* **Select Global banking** (i.e. Parent vs Child banking) - Fundraiser creators on the child site have the ability to choose when creating a new fundraiser, whether the funds should go to the global / central bank account set at the parent level, or a bank account connected to the child site.

* **Parent Site Central Banking + Child Site Users Manage Banking**- In this instance, every fundraiser created on the child site will be prompted to connect a bank account of their choosing that is then connected to their user profile to be used for any subsequent fundraisers. When using this option, the payment gateway connected to the child site must be Stripe.

### Permissions

Permissions are set on a per site basis. Administrators on the parent site however, always have access to Admin reporting for child sites but not actual Admin access on the child sites themselves.

* **Reports**

  * Admin on Parent site can see all reporting for child sites. If a user is only Admin on a child site, they will only be able to see Admin reports for Fundraisers created on that child site.

* **Tax Receipt settings**

  * Tax Receipt settings are entered and managed from the Parent site. This information is pushed down to child sites automatically.

### Creating Fundraisers

When creating fundraisers on a child site, depending on global admin settings (See [**Admin \> General Settings**](admin-general-settings.md)), you may be given the option to "**Only show on the site this campaign was created on**".

If this option is **enabled** , the fundraiser **will not be**mirrored publicly to the Parent site for donors to see. Admins on the Parent site will still see it, but will not be able to edit it or make any changes from the Parent site this must be done from the Child site (sub-site).

If this option is **disabled** , the fundraiser **will be**mirrored publicly to the Parent site, and can be edited from both the parent and child site.  
Editing child-site created fundraisers from the parent site is **not**possible if one of these is true:

* Parent site has custom fields in the "Start A Fundraiser" process.

* Child site has custom fields in the "Start A Fundraiser" process.

* Fundraiser was created from a Master Template.

## Fundraiser Approval on Subsites (Charity Partners)

**NOTE:** These rules only apply to fundraisers that are created from Child sites.

Fundraisers created from Parent sites have no relevance to Child sites, so these rules do not apply.  

| **Parent Approval Enabled** | **Child (Subsite) Approval Enabled** |  **Can be Approved On**  |
|-----------------------------|--------------------------------------|--------------------------|
| Yes                         | No                                   | Parent                   |
| Yes                         | Yes                                  | Either parent or subsite |
| No                          | Yes                                  | Subsite                  |

If you have questions regarding our Parent / Child Relationship, reach out to your dedicated Partner Success Manager, or our customer support team (support@crowdchange.co).

# Fundraiser & Blueprint Custom Tags

For Admins managing CrowdChange sites with many Fundraisers and/or Blueprints in use, we offer the ability to add **Custom Tags**, for easier identification and filtering in Admin Reports.

For example, using this functionality you may tag all fundraisers created in the Summer of 2022 as "**summer-2022** ", then, in the Admin Reports, filter fundraisers based on this tag. Or you could create a tag with the event name and year, example format: `[event-name][year]`*.*

You may apply multiple tags to one fundraiser or Blueprint, as desired.

If a Blueprint is given a tag, then all connected fundraisers will inherit that tag.  
**Please Note:** This feature is **NOT**enabled by default - Reach out to your Partner Success Representative to request it be activated on your CrowdChange site.

## How to Add a Custom Tag to a Fundraiser

To add a custom tag to an individual fundraiser, follow the steps below:

1. Navigate to the fundraiser in question and click **Manage Fundraiser**.

2. On the left sidebar, click **Additional Settings**.

3. Enter your desired tag(s). Press **Enter**to add each tag.

   ![image-20240821-184806.png](../assets/fundraiser-blueprint-custom-tags/image-20240821-184806.png)
4. Scroll down to the bottom and click **Save**.

## How to Add a Custom Tag to a Blueprint

To add a custom tag to a Master Template, follow the steps below:

1. From anywhere on your CrowdChange site, click **Profile** then**Admin**.

2. Navigate to**Blueprints**using the left sidebar.

3. Find the Blueprint in question and click on it.

4. Click the **General Settings** tab.

5. Scroll down and click **Next**. Do this again on the next page.

6. On the last page, scroll down to **Tags**.

7. Enter your desired tag(s). Click **Add**to input each tag.

   ![image-20240208-150930.png](../assets/fundraiser-blueprint-custom-tags/image-20240208-150930.png)
8. Set your desired permissions via the '**This setting can be changed by**' dropdown.

9. Scroll down to the bottom of the page and click **Save**.

## Filtering by Custom Tags

Once custom tags have been added to your fundraisers and/or Blueprints, you will be able to filter by these tags within Admin Reports. For the majority of Admin Reports, in the web version you will see a new field within **Filters** called **Fundraiser tags.**Here you can enter the specific tags you'd like to filter for:  
![testtags.png](../assets/fundraiser-blueprint-custom-tags/testtags.png)

Click **Show Results** in the bottom right corner, and then only data connected to fundraisers or Blueprints with your specified tags will be shown.  
Note that the **Payout Report** will not show this filter in the web version, however when you download the Excel report, you will be able to filter by custom tags (in the final column of the '**Detailed**' tab).

# Set a custom meta description for fundraiser social sharing

If you need to set a custom meta description for your fundraiser(s), which will be used when sharing to social media platforms (instead of the fundraiser description), you can do so using the steps below.  
Please note that this feature is **NOT**enabled by default - you will need to reach out to your Partner Success Representative if you would like to use it.

Once the feature has been enabled on your site, you will be able to use it in 2 ways:

## Create / Edit Fundraiser Process

When creating or editing a fundraiser, look for the '**Meta Description**' field and enter your desired custom meta description for this fundraiser. It will be used in place of the fundraiser description when sharing to social media platforms.  
![metaz.png](../assets/set-a-custom-meta-description-for-fundraiser-socia/metaz.png)

### Create / Edit Blueprint Process (if Blueprints are enabled)

When creating or editing a Blueprint, enter your desired Meta description for fundraisers created from this blueprint. It will be used in place of the fundraiser description when sharing to social media platforms. You can use the permissions dropdown to determine whether fundraiser creators can edit this themselves.  
![image-20240821-185755.png](../assets/set-a-custom-meta-description-for-fundraiser-socia/image-20240821-185755.png)

# Changing the 'Show my name as' options

If you would like to specify exactly what options are available to donors within the 'Show my name as' field at checkout, we offer the ability to set these options at the Admin, Blueprint or Fundraiser level.  
Please note that this functionality is not enabled by default - Reach out to your Partner Success Representative to request it be enabled on your CrowdChange site.

Once enabled on your site, follow the steps below to set the 'Show my name as' options at the **Admin** level:

1. Go to your CrowdChange site and **Log In**with your Admin credentials.

2. Click **Profile** in the top right corner, then **Admin**.

3. On the left sidebar, click **Fundraisers Settings** , then **Show name as**.

4. From this page, you can enter your own custom display name options for donors to select from.

![shownameas.png](../assets/changing-the-show-my-name-as-options/shownameas.png)
If no custom options are entered, the default list will be used.

*** ** * ** ***

You can also set these options at the **Blueprint** level or at the **Fundraiser**level:

* To set them at the Blueprint level, go to **Admin → Blueprints → Donation Settings → Donor Name Display Settings** (of a specific BP).

* To set them at the Fundraiser level, go to the fundraiser and click **Manage Fundraiser** **→ Donation Settings \> Donor Name Display Settings**.

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/badges-and-milestones | Nav: Badges and Milestones | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# Badges and Milestones

A great way to incentivize fundraising is to set up custom **Badges** and **Milestones**!

**Milestone Notification Emails**can be sent when a Fundraiser, Team or Personal Page reaches certain goals.

For example, when a Fundraiser reaches 50% of it's goal or a personal/team page raises it's first $1,000.  
These emails are sent to the Fundraiser Owner and Personal / Team Page Owners, **NOT** to donors.

**Badges** can be created and linked to Milestones to reward achievers with a virtual prize - they are included in the Milestone Notification Emails, and displayed publicly on the achiever's personal or team page:  
![image-20231103-171752.png](../assets/badges-and-milestones/image-20231103-171752.png)

## Setting up Milestone Notification Emails \& Badges

To customize and provide pre-built templates for Milestone Notification Emails, follow the steps below:

1. Go to **Profile → Admin → Communication Settings → Milestones**.

2. Click **Create milestone** .

3. Name the milestone and **select a trigger** from the '**When**' dropdown (Eg: Page Created, End of an event, Certain amount raised, certain number of donations reached, etc).

4. Select the Group which this milestone applies to (Eg: the Fundraiser owner, a page owner, registrant etc).

5. Enter a specific value which should trigger the milestone.

See the example milestone below which will be sent to page owners when they reach $1000 raised.  
![image-20250723-145552.png](../assets/badges-and-milestones/image-20250723-145552.png)

Now you will have the option of adding a **Badge**to the milestone email. See example screenshot below. This is an awesome way to reward fundraisers for their hard work and support of your cause! You can select from our pre-built badges, or upload your own custom badge image using the pencil icon.  
![image-20250723-145937.png](../assets/badges-and-milestones/image-20250723-145937.png)

Finally, ensure to fill out the **Message Body** section which sets what text will appear in the milestone notification email. See example below.  
If you would prefer not to send an email notification for this milestone, simply toggle on the '**Skip sending email for this milestone**' option.  
![image-20250723-151335.png](../assets/badges-and-milestones/image-20250723-151335.png)

When you are finished creating your milestone email template, click the **Save**button.  
![image-20250723-151423.png](../assets/badges-and-milestones/image-20250723-151423.png)  
Now, when a Fundraiser Owner goes to **Manage Fundraiser → Milestones** , they will be able to click **Create Milestone** and create their own milestones. They can see all active milestones but those set at the Admin level are only editable by Admin users.

## Editing Milestone Notification Emails \& Badges

You can come back to the **Admin** or **Fundraiser Level** Milestones Menus at any time to made adjustments to existing milestones, delete them, or add more.

To access the Admin Milestones Menu, go to **Profile → Admin → Communication Settings → Milestones**.  
![image-20240925-193650.png](../assets/badges-and-milestones/image-20240925-193650.png)

To access the Fundraiser Level Milestones Menu, go to **Manage Fundraiser → Milestones**.  
![image-20250723-151925.png](../assets/badges-and-milestones/image-20250723-151925.png)

# Participant Center

The Participant Center is your central fundraising hub, where you can view and manage all of your fundraisers, personal pages and/or team pages across your CrowdChange site. It gives you a high-level overview of your donor engagement, page strength, milestone achievements and more!  
Please note that this feature is **NOT** enabled by default.

If partners would like to opt in, they can request this via their Partner Success Representative.

To access the Participant Center (once enabled), from anywhere on your CrowdChange site, click the **Participant Center** button in the header at the top of the page, as shown below:  
![participant center.png](../assets/participant-center/participant_center.png)

Within your **Participant Center**, you have the following options (read below):  
![image-20240823-191105.png](../assets/participant-center/image-20240823-191105.png)

* Click **Edit Profile** in the top right corner to access your profile where you can upload a photo or edit your account details (name, email address, etc).

* Click either the **Fundraisers** , **Personal Pages** , or **Teams** tab to view the pages you own.

## Fundraisers Tab

From the **Fundraisers**tab, clicking a fundraiser tile (as shown below) will take you directly to it's public page where you can view or manage it as normal.  
![image-20240823-191243.png](../assets/participant-center/image-20240823-191243.png)

## Personal Pages Tab

On the **Personal Pages** tab, clicking a page tile (as shown below) will take you to that page's **Dashboard**, where you can get insight on the page strength, fundraising activity and milestone achievements.  
![image-20240823-190657.png](../assets/participant-center/image-20240823-190657.png)

### Personal Page Dashboard

Here is what your **Personal Page Dashboard** will look like:  
![image-20240823-190555.png](../assets/participant-center/image-20240823-190555.png)

You can get to the live Personal Page itself from here by clicking**View Page** in the top right corner.

The **Share**button in the top right corner is available for you to share your page via social media or link.  
![image-20250805-210655.png](../assets/participant-center/image-20250805-210655.png)

Within the left sidebar of your page dashboard, you can directly access specific menu options from your personal page, such as your **Page Settings** , **Mailing List** , **Report** , and **Offline Donations** menu.  
![image-20240823-191704.png](../assets/participant-center/image-20240823-191704.png)

Scrolling down within the page dashboard, you can view further metrics as well as your badge progress:  
![metrics1.png](../assets/participant-center/metrics1.png)

#### Activity Information \& Activity Badges

If the Activity Tracker is enabled, personal page dashboards within Participant Center will also show one more section: **Activity Tracker**. This section allows page owners to quickly view their activity progress, badges, and to access Activity Tracker from Participant Center to change or track activities.  
![image-20240823-193113.png](../assets/participant-center/image-20240823-193113.png)  
![image-20240823-193150.png](../assets/participant-center/image-20240823-193150.png)

This **Activity Tracker** sectionwill also be shown on the Personal Page itself.

## Teams Tab

On the **Teams** tab within Participant Center, clicking a team tile (as shown below) will take you to that team's **Dashboard**, where you can see further team details and donor metrics.  
![image-20240823-191816.png](../assets/participant-center/image-20240823-191816.png)

### Team Page Dashboard

Here is what your **Team Page Dashboard** will look like:  
![image-20240823-191926.png](../assets/participant-center/image-20240823-191926.png)

You can get to the Team Page itself from here by clicking**View Team**in the top right corner.

The **Share**button in the top right corner is available for you to share your team page via social media or link.

Within the left sidebar of your Team Page Dashboard, you can directly access specific menu options from your Team page, such as your **Page Settings** , **Mailing List** , **Report** , and **Offline Donations** menu.  
![image-20240823-192007.png](../assets/participant-center/image-20240823-192007.png)

#### Activity Highlights \& Activity Tracker Leaderboard

If the Activity Tracker is enabled, team page dashboards within Participant Center will also show two more sections: **Activity Highlights** and **Activity Tracker Leaderboard**. These sections provide Team Captains with useful information and statistics on the Activity engagement of their team members.  
![image-20240823-192209.png](../assets/participant-center/image-20240823-192209.png)

The **Activity Tracker Leaderboard**will also be shown on the Team Page itself.

# Site Admin Level Options for P2P Pages

We offer some useful management options for P2P pages at the Admin/Site level.

These controls allow you to set exactly what functionality your team and page owners should have access to.

They can be accessed from your Admin Dashboard, and any changes made will affect all Personal and/or Team pages across your site. To access these controls, follow the steps below:

1. From anywhere on your CrowdChange site, go to **Profile → Admin** in the top right corner.

   ![admin1.png](../assets/site-admin-level-options-for-p2p-pages/admin1.png)
2. On the left sidebar that appears, click **Fundraisers Settings** , then **Teams and Pages**.

   ![teamsandpages.png](../assets/site-admin-level-options-for-p2p-pages/teamsandpages.png)
3. From here you can **enable** or **disable**specific features of Teams and/or Personal pages.

   ![image-20240709-162722.png](../assets/site-admin-level-options-for-p2p-pages/image-20240709-162722.png)
4. Additionally, you can enable automation settings to **auto-close** , **auto-archive** and **auto-remove** **custom URLs** for Personal Pages on a certain date or after a certain number of days.

   ![image-20240709-162800.png](../assets/site-admin-level-options-for-p2p-pages/image-20240709-162800.png)
5. Ensure to click **Save**at the bottom when ready to apply changes.

   ![image-20240709-162902.png](../assets/site-admin-level-options-for-p2p-pages/image-20240709-162902.png)

title: Super Teams

# Super Teams

Super Teams is an optional P2P fundraising feature, tailor made for corporate or national fundraising programs. This feature is implemented at the Admin / Site level and exists above regular team pages connected to fundraisers. Super Teams are accessible to fundraisers across an entire CrowdChange site, allowing teams to register within one, larger, Super Team.  
Please note that the Super Teams feature is **NOT** available by default.

Reach out to your Partner Success Representative to discuss how this feature can benefit your event!  
![superteams.png](../assets/super-teams/superteams.png)
As an Admin user, you can create and manage Super Teams from your Admin Dashboard.

* The name 'Super Teams' and all other copy associated with this feature is fully customizable to suit each partner's requirements.

* Management of Super Teams can be passed off to 'Super Team Captains' of your choice.

* 'Super Team Captains' will be able to see Super Team statistics, details and reports within their Participant Center → Super Team dashboards.

* Within the registration process, team creators will have the option to connect their team to a Super Team.

* Custom Questions specific to a Super Team can be set up, which will appear after the team creator selects the Super Team they are connecting their team to.

* There is no public / front-facing indication of the Super Team a standard team or page is connected to, whether in the registration process or on the pages themselves.

## Use Case Example:

> Bayview Bank has a national corporate fundraising program with funds being raised in all provinces. To streamline the fundraising process and make it easier to track key metrics, the Super Team "Bayview Bank" was created.

An example use case of the Super Teams feature is corporate fundraising for Bayview Bank, a (fictional) national bank with branches in all provinces of Canada.

To streamline Bayview's national fundraising campaign, the Super Team - Bayview Bank could be created.

From there, regular teams (created within fundraisers and connected to the Super Team) would be for Bayview Bank's provincial branches.

Bayview Bank would then be able to track fundraising and activity tracking success across their entire program via the Super Team dashboard, leaderboard and reports. E.g. total amount raised, total teams, total pages, total registrants, activity progress, etc.

## How to Create a Super Team \& Add Captains

To get started and create your first Super Team, follow the steps below:

1. From anywhere on your CrowdChange site, click **Profile → Admin**in the top-right corner.

2. On the left sidebar, click **Super Teams** to be taken to the Super Teams dashboard.

3. Click **New Super Team** , fill out the information (title, description, image), and click **Save**.

4. You will be prompted to assign a Super Team Captain. Click **Assign Captain**.

   ![assigncaptain.png](../assets/super-teams/assigncaptain.png)

5. On the Team Captains screen that appears, click **Assign Captain** again.

   ![image-20240227-161746.png](../assets/super-teams/image-20240227-161746.png)
6. Enter the captain's email and click **Assign Captain** a final time.

   ![assigncaptain2.png](../assets/super-teams/assigncaptain2.png)

7. The captain will receive an email invitation to manage the Super Team.

8. You may return to the Super Team → Team Captains menu at any time to add or remove captains.

## Super Team Captains - Viewing Dashboard

The Super Team Captains will get an email inviting them to manage the team, which they accept via email, and then they are taken to their Participant Center → Super Team dashboard. This is where they would come to see an overall view of what's happening across the Super Team, view reports and more.

Once a Super Team Captain has accepted the email invitation, they can access the Super Team Dashboard within their Participant Center using the steps below:

1. From anywhere on your CrowdChange site, click **Participant Center** at the top.

2. Click the **Super Teams** tab.

   ![image-20240307-170049.png](../assets/super-teams/image-20240307-170049.png)
3. Click on a Super Team to view it's **Dashboard**.

   ![image-20240307-170127.png](../assets/super-teams/image-20240307-170127.png)  
   ![image-20240307-170331.png](../assets/super-teams/image-20240307-170331.png)  
   ![image-20240307-170350.png](../assets/super-teams/image-20240307-170350.png)

## Connecting Teams to Super Teams

### During Multi-Registration \> Team Creation Process

At the fundraiser level, during the multi-registration process, when creating a team, team captains may optionally choose a Super Team for their team to be connected to. For example:  
![image-20240307-170904.png](../assets/super-teams/image-20240307-170904.png)

### From Existing Team Page Edit Menu

Team Captains can always connect their team to a Super Team at a later date, within their team settings.  
![image-20240307-171124.png](../assets/super-teams/image-20240307-171124.png)

# Activity Tracker

The CrowdChange **Activity Tracker** feature allows you to create various Activities within your site, connected to fundraising campaigns, which participants can opt into and track progress towards, while achieving [Badges and Milestones](badges-and-milestones.md). Scroll down to see an example use case of this functionality.

It's a great way to increase participant engagement with your campaign and your organization's mission.  
Please note that this feature is **NOT** enabled by default.

To have the Activity Tracker enabled, reach out to your Partner Success Representative today!  
![activitytracker2.png](../assets/activity-tracker/activitytracker2.png)
Activity Tracker Admin Menu

**When Activity Tracker is enabled on your site:**

* Fundraisers have a toggle slider within Advanced Features to enable Activity Tracker. Turning this on allows the fundraiser host to access Activities and enables the fundraiser-level Activity Tracker Report.

* Blueprints (if enabled) have a toggle slider to enable Activity Tracker. Turning this on allows fundraiser hosts using the blueprint to access Activities.

* Activity Tracker setup menu is added to Admin Dashboard under Fundraisers Settings → Activity Tracker.

The **Activity Tracker Admin Report** must also be enabled on your site by a CrowdChange Support Agent. Once enabled, it is added to the Admin Dashboard under Reports → Activity Tracker Report.

**Example Use-Case for Activity Tracker:**
> Nicholas has a personal fundraising page within the "*Jackie's Joyathon* " fundraiser, hosted by "*Run for Joy Canada*". The organization has set up activity challenges leading up to the day of the event such as "Jog for 10 minutes every day" and "Eat 7 fruits/vegetables each week", etc.

Using Activity Tracker on his page, Nicholas can track and publicly show his progress towards these activities.

He can also do so via his Personal Page Dashboard within Participant Center (if enabled).

His activity progress is shown publicly (if desired) within the Activity Tracker block on his personal page.

## Getting Started with Activity Tracker

**Please Note:** You will not be able to follow these instructions until Activity Tracker has been enabled on your site by a CrowdChange Partner Success Representative or Support Agent.

### **Setting up an Activity at the Admin Level (within Admin Dashboard)**

To get started, let's set up an Activity within the Admin Dashboard. Follow the steps below to do so:

1. From anywhere on your CrowdChange site, click **Profile → Admin**.

2. Click **Fundraisers Settings → Activity Tracker**on the left sidebar.

3. Click the **Create Activity**button shown below:

   ![create activity.png](../assets/activity-tracker/create_activity.png)
4. Select the **Activity Basis** (what unit will be measured) in the popup that appears and click **Next**.

   ![activity basis.png](../assets/activity-tracker/activity_basis.png)
5. Fill out all the details of your activity, such as **name** , **description** , and **start/end dates**.

   ![ActivityTracker3.png](../assets/activity-tracker/ActivityTracker3.png)
6. Toggle ON '**Set as open for new fundraisers**' to make this activity available to new fundraisers.

7. Toggle ON '**Publish activity**' to make this activity public as opposed to hidden.

8. If desired, use the **Types**section to specify multiple ways this activity may be tracked.

   ![types3.png](../assets/activity-tracker/types3.png)
9. Set an image for this activity and click **Save**.

   ![imagesave.png](../assets/activity-tracker/imagesave.png)

#### **Setting up Badges \& Milestones for the Activity**

After creating an activity, you will be prompted to add **Badges**for the activity as shown below:  
![addbadges.png](../assets/activity-tracker/addbadges.png)

Click on **Add Badge**and fill out all the required information. See definitions below:

**Details**Section:

* **Title**- The name of the badge you are creating.

* **Badge description** - Descriptive and/or congratulatory text about the badge.

* **Image**- The image of or associated with your badge.

![badge1.png](../assets/activity-tracker/badge1.png)

**Goal**Section:

* **Badge type** - How your badge is earned:

  * **Streak-based**means the badge is earned by tracking the activity/habit 'X' number of days in a row.

  * **Total-based**means the badge is earned by tracking the activity/habit 'X' number of days in total within the start and end dates of the activity.

* **Number of days** - the 'X' number referenced above. This is the number of days necessary to fulfill either the streak-based or total-based achievement as described above.

![goal1.png](../assets/activity-tracker/goal1.png)

**Types**Section: If desired, specify which Types (options for tracking the activity) are connected to this badge.  
![types4.png](../assets/activity-tracker/types4.png)

Before saving, create a **Milestone email**to be sent to the participant on achievement of this Badge:  
![save2.png](../assets/activity-tracker/save2.png)

Click **Save** , and you'll be taken to the Badges menu, where you can return at any time to **Add** or **Edit** badges.  
![activitytracker50.png](../assets/activity-tracker/activitytracker50.png)

Click**Back to Activities**in the top left corner to return to the Activity Tracker Admin menu.

You can return here at any time to **Add** , **Edit** or **Archive**activities.  
![activityadminmenu.png](../assets/activity-tracker/activityadminmenu.png)

### **Enabling Activity Tracker on a New Fundraiser**

Activity Tracker must be enabled on a fundraiser by fundraiser basis. Additionally, to use it fully, P2P fundraising pages must be toggled on. Follow the simple steps below to enable it on a new fundraiser:

1. From the home page of your CrowdChange site, click the **Start a Fundraiser**button.

   ![startfundraiser3.png](../assets/activity-tracker/startfundraiser3.png)
2. On the **General Info** page, fill out all required information and click **Next**.

3. On the **Additional Settings** page, enable some or all of the following under**Peer-to-peer features**:

   1. *Personal fundraising pages*

   2. *Team fundraising pages*

   3. *Personal fundraising pages within teams*

4. Under **Advanced Features** , turn **ON** the **Activity tracker** toggle slider.

   ![activitytracker4.png](../assets/activity-tracker/activitytracker4.png)
5. Click **Create Fundraiser**at the bottom of the page.

### **Enabling Activity Tracker on an Existing Fundraiser**

Activity Tracker must be enabled on a fundraiser by fundraiser basis. Additionally, to use it fully, P2P fundraising pages must be toggled on. Follow the simple steps below to enable it on an existing fundraiser:

1. While logged in, go to your fundraiser and click **Manage Fundraiser**.

   ![managem.png](../assets/activity-tracker/managem.png)
2. Click **Peer to Peer features**on the left sidebar.

3. Enable some or all of the following under**Peer-to-peer features**:

   1. *Personal fundraising pages*

   2. *Team fundraising pages*

   3. *Personal fundraising pages under a team can be created (within Personal fundraising pages)*

4. Scroll down and click **Save**.

5. On the left sidebar, click **Activity Tracker**.

6. Enablethe **Activity tracker** toggle slider.

   ![image-20240821-191235.png](../assets/activity-tracker/image-20240821-191235.png)
7. Click **Save**to confirm.

### **Setting up an Activity at the Fundraiser Level**

Activities can also be set up at the individual fundraiser level (once Activity Tracker has been enabled on both the site and the specific fundraiser) by following these steps:

1. While logged in, go to your fundraiser and click **Manage Fundraiser**.

   ![managem.png](../assets/activity-tracker/managem.png)
2. Click **Activity Tracker**on the left sidebar.

3. Scroll down and click the **Create Activity**button.

   ![image-20240821-191358.png](../assets/activity-tracker/image-20240821-191358.png)
4. Select the **Activity Basis** (what unit will be measured) in the popup that appears and click **Next**.

   ![activity basis.png](../assets/activity-tracker/activity_basis.png)
5. Fill out all the details of your activity, such as **name** , **description** , and **start/end dates**.

6. Set Types (if applicable) and an image for the activity and click **Save**.

#### **Setting up Badges \& Milestones for the Activity**

After creating an activity, you will be prompted to add **Badges**for the activity:

1. Click on **Add Badge**and fill out all the required information.

   ![addbadge.png](../assets/activity-tracker/addbadge.png)
2. Before saving, create a **Milestone email**under 'Message content' to be sent to the participant on achievement of this Badge.

3. Click **Save** , and you'll be taken to the Badges menu, where you can return at any time to **Add** or **Edit** badges.

4. Click**Back to Activities**in the top left corner to return to the Activity Tracker menu.

5. You can return here at any time to **Add** , **Edit** or **Archive**activities.

# Opting in to an Activity and Tracking Progress

As a participant to a fundraising campaign with your own personal fundraising page, you have the ability to opt into any Activities created at the Admin or Fundraiser level via your Participant Center.  
On fundraisers using our multi-registration workflow, registrants can also opt-in during this process.

Follow the simple steps below to select and track an activity:

1. Go to your **Participant Center** (click the button at the top of your page).

   ![participantbtn.png](../assets/opting-in-to-an-activity-and-tracking-progress/participantbtn.png)
2. Click the **Personal Pages** tab under your name.

   ![img22.png](../assets/opting-in-to-an-activity-and-tracking-progress/img22.png)
3. Click on your specific personal page tile.

   ![tile.png](../assets/opting-in-to-an-activity-and-tracking-progress/tile.png)
4. Scroll down to the **Activity Tracker** section.

5. Click **See all available activities** , or the **Start tracking** buttonon an activity shown.

   ![test222.png](../assets/opting-in-to-an-activity-and-tracking-progress/test222.png)
   1. If you clicked **See all available activities** , click the**Start Tracking**button on the specific activity you would like to track progress towards. You may only track one activity at a time.

      ![select.png](/__attachments/a_68760b77100ca588ca784079fb7e5ebf9fd59b6fee2be0f0649395681f788dc6/select.png?cb=76038618c94fe70bdc5c453b0b641228)
6. On the activity page, you can click the **Start Tracking** button, then the **Track Activity**button to track your first repetition of the activity:

   ![starttt.png](../assets/opting-in-to-an-activity-and-tracking-progress/starttt.png)
   Start tracking  
   ![track.png](../assets/opting-in-to-an-activity-and-tracking-progress/track.png)
   Track activity
7. Track activities consistently without missing a day to earn a streak, which will count towards **Badges and Milestones** ! Badges and Milestones can also be linked to a **total**reached instead of a streak if desired.

   ![streaks.png](../assets/opting-in-to-an-activity-and-tracking-progress/streaks.png)

Some activities are**total-based** rather than**streak-based**, meaning that even if you miss a day, all days tracked within the activity time period will still count towards Badges and Milestones.

Any time you reach a **Milestone** set at the Activity level, you will receive a Milestone Notification Email and any associated **Badge**, which will live within your Participant Center and if desired, publicly on your page.  
![badges2.png](../assets/opting-in-to-an-activity-and-tracking-progress/badges2.png)

## How to Hide Activity Progress

If you do not want your Activity progress to be displayed publicly on your personal fundraising page, follow the steps below to disable this feature:

1. Go to your **Participant Center** (click the button at the top of your page).

2. Click the **Personal Pages** tab.

3. Click on your personal page tile.

4. Scroll down to the **Activity Tracker** section.

5. Click **Manage Activity**on the activity you are tracking.

6. Scroll down to the bottom of the page and disable the '**Show Activity tracker on my page**' toggle.

![privacy.png](../assets/opting-in-to-an-activity-and-tracking-progress/privacy.png)

# Connecting with Strava

If you already use Strava to track your fitness activity, you can quickly connect your Strava account to CrowdChange so that tracked activity going forward is also tracked in CrowdChange.  
Please note that our Strava integration only works with distance based Activities (km or miles).

Once enabled, all supported data from your Strava activities (**going forward**) is automatically transferred to your selected activity within the CrowdChange Activity Tracker.

Here's how you can set this up!

## How to Connect to Strava

1. Go to your **Participant Center** (click the icon at the top of your screen).

   ![participantbtn.png](../assets/connecting-with-strava/participantbtn.png)
2. Click the **Personal Pages** tab under your name.

   ![img22.png](../assets/connecting-with-strava/img22.png)
3. Click on your specific personal page tile.

   ![tile.png](../assets/connecting-with-strava/tile.png)
4. Scroll down to the **Activity Tracker** section (Your Current Activity will be shown).

   ![image-20250118-205050.png](../assets/connecting-with-strava/image-20250118-205050.png)
5. Click **Manage Activity** (pictured bottom right above).

6. You will be taken to the Activity Tracker Dashboard of your personal page.

   ![image-20250118-205207.png](../assets/connecting-with-strava/image-20250118-205207.png)
7. Click **Connect with Strava** (pictured above).

8. You will be redirected to Strava's website where you must log in to your Strava account.

   ![image-20250118-205317.png](../assets/connecting-with-strava/image-20250118-205317.png)
9. You will then be prompted to authorizethe required permissions for the integration to function.

   ![image-20250117-214013.png](../assets/connecting-with-strava/image-20250117-214013.png)
10. Click **Authorize**and you will be redirected to CrowdChange where you will see Strava is now connected.

    ![connected2.png](/__attachments/a_c2061f42c6e3eda5d5aad18db551ec6273578a66b45fa180254f49c46c076658/connected2.png?cb=fb6f7dbcfa29b82bf499efda9c78a800)

Distance based entries you make in Strava will now be automatically reflected within your CrowdChange Activity Tracker.

# Editing or Deleting Activity Records

Participants have the ability to **Edit** or **Delete**any records previously entered in the Activity Tracker.

This functionality is available for all metric types (Days, Hours and Distance).

Follow the simple steps below in order to to edit or delete a record.

## To Edit a Record

1. Go to your **Personal Page** and scroll down to the**Activity Tracker** section.

2. Click **Manage Activity**.

3. Under **My Records** click **See more records**.

4. Click the **triple-dot icon** next to the record you want to edit and click **Edit**.

5. Make the necessary changes and click **Save**.

## To Delete a Record

1. Go to your **Personal Page** and scroll down to the**Activity Tracker** section.

2. Click **Manage Activity**.

3. Under **My Records** click **See more records**.

4. Click the **triple-dot icon** next to the record you want to delete and click **Delete**.

5. Click **Yes**.

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/activity-tracker-reporting | Nav: Activity Tracker > Activity Tracker Reporting | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# Activity Tracker Reporting

The Activity Tracker is complete with reporting functionality, allowing you to get a bird's eye view of participant engagement with your campaign's Activities.  
**Please note** that the Admin Activity Tracker Report is **NOT** enabled by default and must first be enabled by your CrowdChange Partner Success Representative or Support Agent.

## **Admin Activity Tracker Report**

To view the Admin Activity Tracker Report, follow the steps below:

1. Go to your CrowdChange site and **Log In**.

2. Click **Profile** in in the top right corner, then**Admin**.

3. Navigate to **Reports** **→ Activity Tracker Report**using the left sidebar.

   ![activitytrackerreport.png](../assets/activity-tracker-reporting/activitytrackerreport.png)
4. If needed, you can then **Search** and/or **Filter** for specific activities, and get the Excel version of this report by clicking **Download**.

The downloaded file will contain a **Macro** and **Micro**version of the report.

* The **Macro**version displays activity tracking data on an activity-by-activity basis.

* The **Micro**version displays activity tracking data on a user-by-user basis.

### **Fundraiser Level Activity Tracker Report**

To view the Fundraiser Level Activity Tracker Report, follow the steps below:

1. From anywhere on your CrowdChange site, **Log In**.

2. Go to your fundraising page and click **Manage Fundraiser**.

3. Go to**Reports** on the left sidebar, then**Activity Tracker Report**.

4. From here, you can **Search** and/or **Filter** for specific Activities, and view a simple overview.

   ![report2.png](../assets/activity-tracker-reporting/report2.png)
5. You may also export this report to Excel using the **Download**button.

Note that the fundraiser-level version of this report is less detailed than the Admin version.

# Event Blueprints

The **Event Blueprints** feature allows you to create templates and use them in several ways:

* Manage locations across your signature event from one centralized space, and push changes to your locations post-launch.

* Generate many fundraisers instantly from a single blueprint (template).

* Make blueprints available or required for use by fundraiser creators on your site.

* Control what level of access fundraiser creators have to alter the created fundraisers.

It is a very powerful tool for fundraising at scale and is excellent for:

1. **Signature Event Management** - Event Blueprints makes it simple to set up large scale, multi-location fundraising campaigns. For example, a nation-wide event with satellite locations in all provinces or cities. You can generate all your location pages instantly using our CSV upload option, and add more manually at any time entering just the basic information required by your blueprint.

2. **Community Fundraising** - If you manage community fundraising, Event Blueprints can be a great tool to streamline the fundraising process for your community fundraisers. You can create templates for your community fundraisers to use, and make it required or optional to use them. You can also set the level of flexibility your community fundraisers will have with regards to fundraiser configuration and customization.

*Please note tha* t this feature is **NOT**enabled by default - Reach out to your Partner Success Representative if you would like to use it.

**When setting up an Event Blueprint:**

1. You control which fields fundraiser creators will be allowed to edit, and which fields will be locked.

2. You have the ability to instantly generate multiple fundraisers - as many as you need, based on the Blueprint, and assign fundraiser owners in the same process. This is very useful for large scale, or national events, where a single CrowdChange fundraiser page would be used for one location of an event. For example: One for each city in Canada.

![bps.png](../assets/event-blueprints/bps.png)

## Setting up an Event Blueprint in Admin Settings

Once **Event Blueprints**have been enabled on your CrowdChange site, you can go ahead and set up your first one! Follow these simple steps to get started:

1. From anywhere on your CrowdChange site, click **Profile → Admin**in the top right corner.

2. Click **Blueprints**on the left sidebar.

3. Click **Create New Blueprint**.

4. Fill out the event information in the same way you would for a single fundraiser, however, **note the additional permissions sections** which allow you to give fundraiser creators/owners the ability to edit a given field. *Set to 'Anybody' if fundraiser owners/creators should be able to adjust this setting.*

   ![etg1.png](../assets/event-blueprints/etg1.png)
5. Toggle on your desired**Purchase Options** (Tickets, Apparel/Merch, Registration, Sponsorships, Custom Questions etc), and click **Next**.

   ![image-20240116-155918.png](../assets/event-blueprints/image-20240116-155918.png)
6. Set up **Personal** and **Team** fundraising pages if desired, configure their settings, and click **Next**.

   ![image-20240116-160124.png](../assets/event-blueprints/image-20240116-160124.png)  
   ![image-20240116-160143.png](../assets/event-blueprints/image-20240116-160143.png)
7. On the last page, you can configure**Donation Settings** and other advanced features, as desired.

   ![image-20240116-160324.png](../assets/event-blueprints/image-20240116-160324.png)
8. At the bottom of the page, click **Save** to finalize and create the blueprint.

You can return to the **Profile → Admin → Blueprints** menu at any time and click on a blueprint to **Edit** it,**Archive** it, adjust its **Purchase Options** , **Donation Amounts** , **Email Templates** , **P2P settings** , and set up the **fundraiser blocks** for it's connected child events.

You can also make the blueprint **private** (Only accessible by Admins) or **public** (Accessible to any fundraiser creator) using **Set to public** or **Set to private** within the **triple-dot icon**menu (top-right).

See an example blueprint below with all of these options available:  
![image-20240823-184435.png](../assets/event-blueprints/image-20240823-184435.png)  
If you want to make it **mandatory** for fundraiser creators on your site to use an Event Blueprint, you can go to **Profile → Admin** (**General Settings** page), and toggle on **Users can start fundraisers only from templates** . *Note that at least one blueprint must be set to* ***Public*** *for this option to show.*

## Setting up Fundraiser Blocks within a Blueprint

When setting up a Blueprint you can also choose how the fundraiser blocks will appear on the individual fundraisers, and what permissions fundraiser owners will have to make changes to them.

To do so, follow the steps below:

1. From anywhere on your CrowdChange site, click **Profile → Admin** in the top right corner.

2. Click **Blueprints** on the left sidebar.

3. Click the Blueprint you would like to set this for.

4. Click **Design your fundraiser**.

   ![designit.png](../assets/event-blueprints/designit.png)
5. You will be taken to a preview in Manage Fundraiser Mode, where you can add, edit, or remove the blocks, adjust the Hero image, theme settings, and set access permissions for fundraiser owners.

   ![image-20240124-162942.png](../assets/event-blueprints/image-20240124-162942.png)  
   ![image-20240117-133817.png](../assets/event-blueprints/image-20240117-133817.png)
6. Click **General Permissions**in the top left of the page to adjust the overall block and theme permissions.

   ![image-20240117-134033.png](../assets/event-blueprints/image-20240117-134033.png)
7. Within each block, and the Hero image, you will see a **Permissions**option which lets you decide if the fundraiser owner should be able to make changes to these components.

   ![set perm.png](../assets/event-blueprints/set_perm.png)  
   ![perm2.png](../assets/event-blueprints/perm2.png)
8. When finished, scroll to the top and click**Back to Dashboard** , or if you'd like, you can click **Switch to view mode**first to see a preview of how the fundraisers will look live.

   :back:

## Generating Fundraisers from a Blueprint

You have the ability to generate fundraisers instantly from the Blueprint you have just created.

This is done quickly and efficiently via a **CSV upload** with all of the basic information for each fundraiser.

Once you've set up your Blueprint, to generate multiple fundraisers at once, follow these steps:

1. From anywhere on your CrowdChange site, click **Profile → Admin**in the top right corner.

2. Click **Blueprints**on the left sidebar.

3. Click on a blueprint, then click **Fundraisers management** on the left sidebar.

4. Click the **Manage**button in the top right corner.

   ![manage.png](../assets/event-blueprints/manage.png)
5. Download the .CSV template file which already contains the required headers for your .CSV upload.

   ![downloadz.png](../assets/event-blueprints/downloadz.png)
6. Upload your .CSV file with the required headers and information.

   ![upload.png](../assets/event-blueprints/upload.png)
7. Click **Proceed with uploaded file** when ready.

   ![uploaded.png](../assets/event-blueprints/uploaded.png)
8. Confirm the creation of the fundraisers in your CSV by clicking **Add new events**.

   ![addnewevents.png](../assets/event-blueprints/addnewevents.png)

## Fundraiser Creators using Blueprints

For fundraiser creators on your site, the process of using Blueprints is easy!

Here are instructions you can give them:

1. From the home page, click **Start a Fundraiser**.

2. Select an existing **Blueprint**.

3. Fill out all required, editable information and click **Create Fundraiser**.

## Editing an Individual Fundraiser created from a Blueprint

A fundraiser created from a Blueprint can be edited just like any other fundraiser, however, fields or blocks which were locked for editing when the Blueprint was created will be locked, unless the Blueprint is changed.

To edit the individual fundraiser's settings:

1. Go to the fundraiser and click **Manage Fundraiser → General settings.**

2. Make any updates needed, scroll down and click **Save**.

3. Click **Additional Settings** on the left sidebar.

4. Make any updates needed, scroll down and click **Save Changes**.

The fundraiser blocks can be edited in the same way, according to the access provided at the blueprint level.

## Editing a Blueprint and pushing changes to all its fundraisers

You have the ability to edit a Blueprint at any time, and by enabling the **Force update on all fundraisers** toggle next to each option / field within the edit menu, your changes will be pushed to all connected fundraisers immediately after clicking **Save Changes**.

To make and push changes, follow these steps:

1. From anywhere on your CrowdChange site, click **Profile → Admin**.

2. Click **Blueprints**on the left sidebar.

3. Click the blueprint you would like to edit.

4. Click **General Settings** , make all desired changes, and for changes you want to push out to connected fundraisers, ensure to enable the **Force update on all fundraisers**toggle underneath that field.

   1. *For features that were not previously enabled, you must also set the access permissions so that the fundraiser owner may toggle the new feature on ("This setting can be changed by 'Anybody'").*

      ![forceup.png](/__attachments/a_0e2f488a48f26ae1fc96ab6f32bccdc889f20758582209bcc64a4a3bccfc236d/forceup.png?cb=7dcd047323ab5d4324cefdff96864771)
5. Scroll down and click **Next** on each page, then **Save**on the last, and your changes will be pushed out.

All settings and features of your Blueprint (Purchase options, Donation Settings, Email Templates, Team \& Personal Page Custom Questions, etc) can be adjusted at your convenience within the Blueprint dashboard.

# Blueprint Child Event Permissions

Within each Blueprint, there is a dedicated permissions page for child events, allowing you to set exactly which controls are available to non-admin fundraiser owners.

This provides flexible, granular access control for organization Admins managing large campaigns.

To access this page within a Blueprint, follow the steps below:

1. From anywhere on your CrowdChange site, click **Profile → Admin** in the top right corner.

   ![profileadmin.png](../assets/blueprint-child-event-permissions/profileadmin.png)
2. On the left sidebar, click **Blueprints** .

   ![image-20250723-152157.png](../assets/blueprint-child-event-permissions/image-20250723-152157.png)
3. Click on the specific blueprint.

   ![image-20250723-152615.png](../assets/blueprint-child-event-permissions/image-20250723-152615.png)
4. Click **Child Events Permissions**on the bottom-left within the Blueprint dashboard.

   ![image-20250723-152724.png](../assets/blueprint-child-event-permissions/image-20250723-152724.png)
5. On the **Child Events Permissions** page, you will be able to set the access controls.

   ![image-20250723-152851.png](../assets/blueprint-child-event-permissions/image-20250723-152851.png)
6. When you are finished adjusting the settings, click Save.

   ![image-20250723-153135.png](../assets/blueprint-child-event-permissions/image-20250723-153135.png)

**Please Note:**

Setting to **Anyone** means that fundraiser owners will be able to change it.

Setting to **Admin** means only site Admins will be able to change it.

Setting to **No one** means no one will be able to change it.

# Site Communication

The **Site Communication** feature is used to create site-wide communication messages for things like updates, warnings, notifications, general information, and more.

It provides an easy and efficient way to quickly communicate important knowledge to users on your site.

Messages can be targeted to the Homepage, Participant Center, Fundraisers and/or P2P Pages.  
![test22222.png](../assets/site-communication/test22222.png)

For example, you can inform users of a significant milestone reached, give them instructions on how to take certain actions, provide a link to register for your major event, and much more! Feel free to get creative.  
Please note that this feature is **NOT**enabled by default - Reach out to your Partner Success Representative today to have it enabled on your site!

Once the feature has been enabled on your CrowdChange site, follow the steps below to create a message:

1. While logged in, click **Profile** in the top right corner, then **Admin**.

2. Click **Communication Settings → Site Communications**on the left sidebar.

3. Click **Create message**.

4. Enter the title and body text of your message (in French as well if site is bilingual).

5. Select an icon (Info, Success, Warning, Error).

   ![createmg.png](../assets/site-communication/createmg.png)
6. Check the **Allow users to close this message** box if desired.

7. Enter a date range for when the message will be shown, if desired.

8. Under **Target Pages** , click **Advanced settings** to customize exactly where this message will be shown. If this step is skipped, the message will be shown on all pages.

9. Click **Save**.

*** ** * ** ***

You may return to the Site Communication menu at any time to add, update, archive or delete messages.  
![sitecomms.png](../assets/site-communication/sitecomms.png)

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/how-to-issue-full-and-partial-refunds | Nav: How to Issue Full and Partial Refunds | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# How to Issue Full and Partial Refunds

Need to refund a transaction? CrowdChange now provides the ability for Admins to issue **Partial Refunds**in addition to standard, full refunds. For example, you can refund 2 tickets only, out of a transaction of 5 tickets.

Partial Refunds are a convenient tool in situations where a donor or supporter requests a refund for a specific part of their transaction - Instead of having to refund the entire transaction and potentially lose that revenue (if they decide not to re-donate), you can simply refund the specific item they requested.

To issue a refund of either kind, follow these simple steps:

1. Go to your CrowdChange site and **Log In**.

2. Click **Profile** in in the top right corner, then**Admin**.

3. Go to **Reports** **→ Donations Report**using the left sidebar.

4. Click on the transaction you would like to refund (fully or partially).

5. Click the grey **Refund**button in the bottom right corner of the transaction's menu.

6. Check the box next to the items you would like to refund, and enter a comment, as shown below:

   ![image-20231103-180137.png](../assets/how-to-issue-full-and-partial-refunds/image-20231103-180137.png)
   (Example partial refund of 2 tickets (and covered fees) from a 5 ticket transaction.)
7. Click **Refund**in the bottom right corner to complete the refund process.

*** ** * ** ***

**Please Note:** Refunds will be listed separatelyin the Admin Donations Report, but transactions which have been partially refunded will also show this information within their transaction panel.  
![image-20231103-175410.png](../assets/how-to-issue-full-and-partial-refunds/image-20231103-175410.png)
Admin Donations Report listing both the initial transaction and the refund.  
![image-20231103-175458.png](../assets/how-to-issue-full-and-partial-refunds/image-20231103-175458.png)
If you click the initial transaction, within its transaction panel you will see information on the refund...  
![image-20231103-175435.png](../assets/how-to-issue-full-and-partial-refunds/image-20231103-175435.png)
...and specifics on which components of the transaction were refunded.

The **Fundraiser-Level Donations Report** will also show partial refunds within transactions.  
![refundsz.png](../assets/how-to-issue-full-and-partial-refunds/refundsz.png)  

## **Tax Receipts \& Partial Refunds**

See three examples below of how Tax Receipting interacts with Partial Refunds:

### **Example #1** : Initial transaction of $50 includes a $15 donation, and a $35 registration purchase. The organization's minimum donation amount for issuing a Tax Receipt is $20.

→ Therefore, a Tax Receipt for $50 is initially issued with this transaction.

→ An Admin user refunds the $35 registration tier, as the donor is no longer able to participate in the event. The donor receives a $35 refund, and the initial Tax Receipt is now void as the remaining $15 donation does not meet the organization's minimum amount required to receive a receipt.

### **Example #2** :Initial transaction of $100 includes a $50 donation, and a $50 ticket. The organization's minimum donation amount for issuing a Tax Receipt is $20.

→ Therefore, a Tax Receipt for $100 is initially issued with this transaction.

→ An Admin user refunds the $50 ticket, as the donor is no longer able to attend this event. The donor receives a $50 refund, the initial Tax Receipt is voided and a new Tax Receipt is generated, then issued, to the donor for the new tax-eligible amount of $50.

### **Example #3** : Initial transaction of $100 includes a $50 donation, and a $50 ticket which was not deemed tax eligible. The organization's minimum donation amount for issuing a Tax Receipt is $20.

→ A Tax Receipt for $50 is initially issued with this transaction.

→ An Admin user refunds the $50 ticket, as the donor is no longer able to attend this event. The donor receives a $50 refund, and the initial Tax Receipt is unaffected as the ticket price was not originally part of the tax-eligible amount.

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/note-on-refunds-for-sites-with-multi-registration | Nav: How to Issue Full and Partial Refunds > Note on Refunds for Sites with Multi-Registration | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# Note on Refunds for Sites with Multi-Registration

This section applies only to sites with our **Multi-Registration** flow enabled.

## Issuing Refunds

During the regular [**Refund**](how-to-issue-full-and-partial-refunds.md)process, you can also refund (multi-)registration transactions, including self-donations, made during the registration process. In order to do so, follow these steps:

1. Go to the **Admin Donations Report**(Profile \> Admin \> Reports \> Donations Report), and select the correct transaction.

2. Click the **Refund** button in the bottom right of the menu that appears.

3. Select the specific items you want to refund, check amounts and enter a reason for the refund.

4. Your chosen items will be refunded. This may affect items created or used during the initial transaction (teams, pages, tickets, etc).

**Regarding P2P Pages created from Registration:**

When you refund a **Registration** (even a free one), it will delete the fundraising page made during the registration process. This will **not** refund the donation, made during multi-registration.

If you want to refund the donation made during the multi-registration process, you must select the correct entry under the "**Self Donations**" block.

Refunding only the donation, made during multi-registration, will **not** delete the attached fundraising page and will **not** refund the registration ticket price.

So, in order to fully refund everything a person paid for a single registration during the multi-registration process, you must refund both the "**Registration** " and "**Self Donations**" blocks.

# Recommended Web Browsers & Versions

CrowdChange is compatible with all modern web browsers. To ensure you get the best experience possible, we recommend using the most up-to-date version of one of the following:  

| **Browser** |         **Recommended Versions**          |
|-------------|-------------------------------------------|
| Chrome      | Latest                                    |
| Firefox     | Latest and extended support release (ESR) |
| Edge        | 2 most recent major versions              |
| Safari      | 2 most recent major versions              |
| iOS         | 2 most recent major versions              |
| Android     | 2 most recent major versions              |

Being a cloud platform, our software does not run natively on user devices. It is simply accessed via a web browser. Therefore we do not have specific Operating System requirements.
