# Donation Progress Block - how to track amount raised and goals on your fundraiser

The **Donation progress block** displays key fundraising metrics on your fundraiser page, including the total amount raised, your goal (if enabled), and optional totals like **Raised by teams** , **Raised by pages** , and **Donors**.

This block now supports **stretch goals**, meaning that if your fundraiser exceeds its goal, the progress indicator can display progress above 100%, and you can optionally show a "goal exceeded" celebration hint and customize the exceeded progress colors.

If your fundraiser has a goal enabled, it will be shown in the **Donation progress block** . If you elect to display this block without a goal set, it will count **overall funds raised**, without showing a goal.  
![image-20260304-150241.png](../assets/donation-progress-block-how-to-track-amount-raised/image-20260304-150241.png)
The **Donation progress block** on a peer-to-peer fundraiser

*** ** * ** ***

## How to edit the Donation progress block

To edit the Donation progress block, follow the below steps:

* Go to your CrowdChange page and Log in

* Once on the fundraiser you would like to edit, click **Manage fundraiser**

* Once on the Fundraiser dashboard, click **Design your fundraiser**

* Scroll to the **Donation progress** block, and click the **Edit** button

* Make your updates (Layout, Appearance, Content, etc.)

* Click **Save** to publish your changes

*** ** * ** ***

## How to add a Donation progress block

If your fundraiser is missing a Donation progress block, it is possible it was previously deleted. To restore it, please follow these steps:

* Go to your CrowdChange page and Log in

* Once on the fundraiser you would like to edit, click **Manage fundraiser**

* Once on the Fundraiser dashboard, click **Design your fundraiser**

* Within the user interface, between any two blocks, click the **Plus** icon

* The list of available blocks will then be shown, select the **Donation progress** block

* Click **Save** if prompted

*** ** * ** ***

## Layout options

Within the **Layout** section, you can control how the Donation progress block is displayed on the page:

* **One column** - Displays your fundraising progress in a single, streamlined section.

* **Two columns** - Displays a larger primary panel on the left (for example, total raised and the progress chart) and a secondary panel on the right for additional stats (for example, raised by teams, raised by pages, donors).

### Primary block

The **Primary block** is the main metric shown in the Donation progress block. In the **Raised amounts** section, you can choose to display:

* **Raised amount**

* **Goal**

If the **Goal** is enabled, you can edit the goal amount directly in this panel. Please note, updating this goal value will also update the fundraiser goal in the fundraiser's **General settings**.

### Secondary blocks

The **Secondary blocks** section allows you to show or hide additional fundraising stats, such as:

* **Raised by teams**

* **Raised by pages**

* **Donors**

You can toggle each secondary block on or off. If needed, you can also promote a secondary stat to be the main display by selecting **Make primary**.

*** ** * ** ***

## Stretch goals and goal exceeded settings

When your fundraiser exceeds its goal, the Donation progress block can visually display progress beyond 100% (for example, 115%), which supports stretch goal momentum and helps communicate that the campaign is continuing to grow.

Within the **Appearance** settings, you can also enable and customize:

* **Celebrate goal reached** - Shows a celebration confetti effect when the goal is reached.

* **Exceeded goal hint** - Displays a short celebration label near the progress chart when the goal is exceeded (the text is customizable, and is designed for short messages like "Goal exceeded!" or a stretch goal callout).

* **Exceeded progress bar color** - Allows you to set a separate color for the exceeded portion of the progress bar or chart, making stretch progress visually distinct from standard progress.

Tip: If you are testing these settings while editing, use the fundraiser preview in the **Design your fundraiser** view to confirm how the goal reached and goal exceeded states look before publishing.

*** ** * ** ***

## Appearance

The **Appearance** section controls how the Donation progress block looks, including the progress visualization and colors.

### Progress bar style

You can choose between:

* **Donut chart** - A circular progress chart, ideal for highlighting percent-to-goal.

* **Horizontal bar** - A more traditional progress bar display.

### Color settings

You can also customize:

* Background color

* Primary block background color and text color

* Secondary block background color and text color

* Progress bar color

* Filled progress bar color

* Exceeded progress bar color (stretch goals)

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/gallery-block-how-to-add-an-image-gallery-to-the-b | Nav: Gallery Block - How to add an image gallery to the body of your fundraising page | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# Gallery Block - How to add an image gallery to the body of your fundraising page

The **Gallery block** allows you to add a photo gallery directly within the body of your fundraiser page. This is a great way to showcase event photos, highlight your impact, recognize sponsors, or add visual storytelling throughout your campaign.

You can upload **up to 20 images** into a single Gallery block, customize the gallery title, select a layout style, and adjust basic colour settings to match your fundraiser branding.  
![image-20260304-153059.png](../assets/gallery-block-how-to-add-an-image-gallery-to-the-b/image-20260304-153059.png)
The **Gallery block** using the **Modular** layout

*** ** * ** ***

## How to add a Gallery block

The **Gallery block**is not enabled by default. To add a Gallery block, please follow these steps:

* Go to your CrowdChange page and **Log in**

* Once on the fundraiser you would like to edit, click **Manage fundraiser**

* Once on the Fundraiser dashboard, click **Design your fundraiser**

* Within the user interface, between any two blocks, click the **Plus** icon

* The list of available blocks will then be shown, select the **Gallery block**

*** ** * ** ***

## Content - how to set your gallery title and upload images

Within the **Content** section of the Gallery block editor, you can:

### Gallery title

* Update the **Gallery title** (for example, "Event Photos", "Impact Highlights", or "In the Community")

* If left as-is, the default title will display as **Gallery**

### Images

In the **Images** section, you can upload the photos you want displayed in the gallery.

Supported file rules:

* Accepted formats: **JPG, PNG, GIF**

* Maximum number of images: **20**

* Maximum file size: **25MB per image**

Tip: For the best visual results, use clear, high-resolution images with consistent lighting and similar aspect ratios where possible.

*** ** * ** ***

## Layout - how to choose how your gallery displays

Within the **Layout** section, you can select how your gallery images are arranged on the page. Layout availability may vary depending on your fundraiser setup.

Common layout options include:

* **Modular** - Displays your images in a dynamic grid layout, designed to create a visually engaging gallery with a mix of image sizes.

* **Stack** - Displays images in a simpler stacked layout, ideal for a clean, straightforward photo list.

* **Carousel** - Displays images in a rotating slider format, ideal when you want visitors to browse photos without taking up as much vertical page space.

*** ** * ** ***

## Appearance - how to adjust colours

Within the **Appearance** section of the Gallery block editor, you can customize:

* **Title text color** - Controls the colour of the Gallery title text.

* **Background color** - Controls the background colour behind the gallery block.

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/fundraiser-moderation-approval-smart-fundraiser-protection-admins | Nav: Fundraiser Moderation: Approval & Smart Fundraiser Protection (Admins) | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# Fundraiser Moderation: Approval & Smart Fundraiser Protection (Admins)

CrowdChange provides two complementary systems to help you manage fundraiser quality and prevent spam on your site:

* **Fundraiser Approval** (manual review)

* **Smart Fundraiser Protection** (automated safeguards)

Together, these tools help you balance **control** , **security** , and **fundraiser speed**.

*** ** * ** ***

## 1. Overview

When a fundraiser is created on your site, it may either:

* **Go live instantly**, or

* Be placed in **Pending Approval** for review

This outcome depends on:

* Your **Fundraiser Approval setting**, and

* Whether the fundraiser is **flagged by Smart Fundraiser Protection**

*** ** * ** ***

## 2. Understanding Fundraiser Approval

Fundraiser Approval is a setting that allows your team to **manually review and approve all fundraisers before they go live**.

### When Approval is Enabled

* All new fundraisers are placed in **Pending Approval**

* Fundraisers **cannot accept donations** until approved

### When Approval is Disabled

* Fundraisers typically go live instantly

* Only flagged fundraisers (see below) require approval

*** ** * ** ***

### Benefits of Fundraiser Approval

* Full control over fundraiser content

* Ensures alignment with your organization's brand and policies

* Useful for regulated or high-visibility campaigns

*** ** * ** ***

### Considerations

* Introduces delays before fundraisers can begin

* Requires active monitoring by your team

* May impact fundraiser momentum and participation

*** ** * ** ***

## 3. What is Smart Fundraiser Protection?

Smart Fundraiser Protection is an automated system that reviews fundraisers **at the time of creation** to help prevent spam and suspicious activity.

### What it does

* Automatically evaluates fundraisers using a combination of signals, including:

  * Content quality (e.g., titles and descriptions)

  * Account credibility

  * Email verification status

### What happens next

* **Most fundraisers** → go live instantly

* **Suspicious fundraisers** → are flagged and placed in **Pending Approval**

This ensures that:

* Legitimate fundraisers are not delayed

* Potentially risky fundraisers are reviewed before going live

*** ** * ** ***

## 4. How These Systems Work Together

|  Configuration   |                                 Outcome                                  |
|------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Approval OFF** | Most fundraisers go live instantly; flagged fundraisers require approval |
| **Approval ON**  | All fundraisers require approval before going live                       |

Smart Fundraiser Protection is always active and works in the background.

*** ** * ** ***

## 5. Email Verification \& Account Settings

### Requiring verified accounts to activate fundraisers

By default, a fundraiser must have a **verified email address** before it can go live. This helps keep spam and fake accounts off your site. You can control this behavior in **Admin → General Settings** with the setting:
> **"Users must have verified accounts to activate fundraisers."**

* **Enabled (default):** A new fundraiser stays inactive until its owner verifies their email. The owner sees a "verify your email" prompt with the option to resend the verification email.

* **Disabled:** New fundraisers can activate immediately without waiting for email verification. A verification email is still sent and the prompt still appears, but it no longer blocks the fundraiser from going live. Ownership reassignments also take effect immediately, without requiring the new owner to verify or accept.

Disabling this setting only affects the **email-verification step** . Smart Fundraiser Protection's spam and content safeguards stay active at all times. This option is most useful for organizations that create or reassign fundraisers **on behalf of** their participants.

### Assigning a fundraiser owner (admin-created fundraisers)

When an admin creates a fundraiser, you can set a **Fundraiser owner** by entering that person's email (and name, if they're a new user). The fundraiser owner is set as the **banking owner** for that fundraiser when user-level banking is used.

*** ** * ** ***

## 6. Why a Fundraiser May Be Inactive

An inactive fundraiser is not visible and cannot accept donations. The platform distinguishes between the common reasons so you can resolve them quickly:

* **Pending approval** --- awaiting manual review (see below)

* **Banking not set up** --- the fundraiser's banking details are incomplete

* **Unverified account** --- when the verified-accounts setting is enabled, the owner has not yet verified their email

*** ** * ** ***

## 7. Why a Fundraiser May Require Approval

A fundraiser may appear in **Pending Approval** for several reasons:

* Your organization has **Fundraiser Approval enabled**

* The fundraiser was **flagged by Smart Fundraiser Protection**, due to:

  * Suspicious or inappropriate content

  * Low-confidence user information

  * Lack of verified email

*** ** * ** ***

## 8. How to Approve or Reject a Fundraiser

If a fundraiser requires approval, follow these steps:

1. Go to the **Browse Fundraisers** page on your site

2. Click **Show All** , then select **Pending Approval**

3. Click on the fundraiser you want to review

4. Click **Manage Fundraiser** in the top right corner

5. *(Optional)* Review and update fundraiser details before approval

6. Click **Approve** to make the fundraiser live

To reject a fundraiser:

* Click **Reject** (this will remove the fundraiser from your site)

> **Note:** Once approved, a fundraiser can begin accepting donations immediately.

*** ** * ** ***

## 9. Best Practices

* **Review pending fundraisers regularly** to avoid delays for legitimate users

* Consider setting an internal response time (e.g., within 24 hours)

* If you prioritize speed, consider keeping Approval OFF and relying on Smart Fundraiser Protection

* Use Approval ON for campaigns requiring strict oversight

*** ** * ** ***

## 10. Frequently Asked Questions

### Why did one fundraiser go live instantly and another require approval?

This is expected behavior. Fundraisers that meet quality and trust checks go live instantly, while others may be flagged for review.

*** ** * ** ***

### Can I disable Smart Fundraiser Protection?

The spam and content safeguards (such as blocking inappropriate titles and flagging suspicious content) are platform-level and **cannot be turned off** . However, you *can* control the email-verification requirement: the **"Users must have verified accounts to activate fundraisers"** setting in **Admin → General Settings** lets you choose whether fundraisers must have a verified email before they go live. Disabling that setting does **not** turn off spam protection --- it only allows fundraisers to activate before email verification.

*** ** * ** ***

### What does the "verified accounts" setting do?

When enabled (the default), a fundraiser must have a verified email before it can go live. When disabled, fundraisers can activate immediately and ownership reassignments take effect right away --- useful if your team creates or reassigns fundraisers on behalf of your participants. The verification email is still sent either way.

*** ** * ** ***

### What happens if I don't approve a fundraiser?

The fundraiser will remain in **Pending Approval** and will not be visible or accept donations.

*** ** * ** ***

### Can I edit a fundraiser before approving it?

Yes. You can review and update fundraiser details before approving.

*** ** * ** ***

### What happens when I reject a fundraiser?

Rejecting a fundraiser removes it from your site. This action cannot be undone.

*** ** * ** ***

## 11. Additional Notes

* In some cases, fundraisers can only be edited from the site where they were created

  * For example, if a child site (sub-site) uses custom questions, you may be redirected to that site to make edits

* If a fundraiser is mistakenly approved, you can close it using:

  **How to Reopen or Close a Fundraiser**

*** ** * ** ***

## 12. Summary

CrowdChange's fundraiser moderation system is designed to:

* Keep fundraiser creation **fast and accessible**

* Reduce spam and malicious activity

* Give your team **flexible control** when needed

By combining **Smart Fundraiser Protection** with optional **Fundraiser Approval** --- and the ability to control email-verification requirements --- you can tailor the right balance for your organization.

================================================================================

# Email Center - How to send emails from CrowdChange

The **Email center** allows you to communicate directly with your supporters by managing contacts, creating reusable templates, and sending emails from within your CrowdChange site.

The Email Center is available at the site-wide, fundraiser, team, and personal page levels, making it easy to reach the right audience based on your role.

*** ** * ** ***

## Accessing the Email Center

You can access the Email Center from multiple areas of your dashboard:

* **Fundraiser level** : Click **Manage fundraiser** , then select **Email center** from the left-hand menu.

* **Team or Personal page level** : Click **Manage page/team** , then select **Email center**.

*** ** * ** ***

## Overview

Once inside the Email Center, you will see three main options:

* **Manage contacts**

* **Templates**

* **Send emails**

Each section is designed to help you organize your audience and streamline your communication.

*** ** * ** ***

## Manage Contacts

The **Manage contacts** section allows you to build and organize your email recipient list.

### Adding Contacts

You can add contacts in several ways:

* **Manually**: Add contacts one at a time by entering:

  * First name

  * Last name

  * Email address

  * Preferred notification language (for bilingual sites)

  * Label (if you want to categorize contacts by group)

![image-20260421-133825.png](../assets/email-center-how-to-send-emails-from-crowdchange/image-20260421-133825.png)

* **Import from Google**: Connect your Gmail account to import contacts directly.

* **Upload a CSV file**: Upload a contact list using the provided CSV template. Include each contact's first name, last name, email address, and preferred notification language (enter EN for English or FR for French on bilingual sites).

![image-20260421-133742.png](../assets/email-center-how-to-send-emails-from-crowdchange/image-20260421-133742.png)

### Contact Labels

Contacts may include pre-existing labels to help you organize and filter recipients. These can include:

* Donors

* Previous donors

* Team captains

You can use these labels when selecting recipients for your emails. Custom labels can be added when adding contacts manually.

*** ** * ** ***

## Templates

The **Templates** section allows you to create and reuse email templates for consistent communication.

### Template Availability

Templates can be created at different levels, which determines who can access them:

* **Site-wide templates**: Available across all fundraisers, teams, and personal pages.

* **Fundraiser-level templates**: Available to the fundraiser owner, as well as all teams and personal pages within that fundraiser.

* **Team-level templates**: Available to the team captain and all personal pages within the team.

* **Personal page templates**: Available only to the page owner.

Templates help save time and ensure consistent messaging across your campaign.

*** ** * ** ***

## Send Emails

The **Send emails** section allows you to compose and send messages to your contacts.

### Step 1: Set Sender Information

Before composing your email, you will need to confirm your sender details:

* If your account email is already verified, it will be selected by default.

* If not, you will be prompted to verify your email address.

* You can also add and verify a different sender email if needed.

### Step 2: Create Your Email

You can either:

* Start from scratch, or

* Select an existing template (if available)

You will then be able to:

* Enter a subject line

* Write your message content

If a template is selected, this will also be editable.

If you have created a new email, you can optionally save it as a **Template** for future use.

### Dynamic Tags

Dynamic tags allow you to personalize your emails. For example:

* `{first-name}`

* `{last-name}`

* `{full-name}`

To view all available tags, click **See all available tags** below the message editor.

### Step 3: Select Recipients

After creating your message, click **Next** to choose your recipients.

You can:

* Filter contacts by label (for example, Donors or Team Captains)

* Select individual contacts

* Use the checkbox at the top of the list to select all visible contacts, with the option to select all contacts in your list

### Step 4: Preview and Send

You will be taken to a preview screen where you can:

* Review your message

* Confirm your recipient list

Once ready:

* You can **Schedule**when your email is sent, or leave this toggle off if you want to send instantly

* Complete the reCAPTCHA verification

* Click **Send** to deliver your email

*** ** * ** ***

## Bilingual Behavior

If your CrowdChange site is set to bilingual, the Email Center includes language-specific functionality to ensure recipients receive communications in their preferred language.

* When adding contacts manually or uploading a CSV file, you will be prompted to select a preferred notification language for each contact.

* The **Send preview email** function will always send both the English and French versions of your message to you.

* Recipients will only receive the version of the email that matches their selected language preference.

* Contacts such as Donors, Previous Donors, and Team Captains will have their language set automatically based on the language used when they created their account or made their first donation.

* If a user would like to update their language preference, they can do so through the **Notifications** section of their profile.

================================================================================

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/auctions-how-to-host-an-auction-on-crowdchange | Nav: Auctions - How to host an Auction on CrowdChange | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# Auctions - How to host an Auction on CrowdChange

We're excited to introduce **Auctions**, a new way to bring more energy, engagement, and fundraising potential to your CrowdChange campaigns.

With Auctions, your fundraiser can now go beyond donations, tickets, merchandise, and registrations. You can showcase special items, donated prizes, exclusive experiences, gift baskets, memorabilia, travel packages, and more, all directly from your CrowdChange fundraiser.

Auctions give supporters a reason to come back, check the latest bids, save their favourite items, and stay engaged right up until closing time. Whether you are running a gala, campaign, community event, chapter fundraiser, or online giving initiative, Auctions help turn your fundraiser into a more interactive experience.

*** ** * ** ***

## What Are Auctions?

Auctions allow your organization to run an online auction directly through your existing CrowdChange fundraiser.

Once enabled, supporters can browse auction items, place bids, follow items they are interested in, and receive notifications when there is bidding activity. This creates a fun, competitive way for your community to support your cause while helping your organization raise more from donated items and experiences.  
![image-20260501-174355.png](../assets/auctions-how-to-host-an-auction-on-crowdchange/image-20260501-174355.png)

### Auction formats available

CrowdChange supports a few different auction formats, giving you flexibility based on the type of experience you want to create.

#### Standard Auction

A standard auction shows supporters the current bid and allows them to place a higher bid while the item is open.

This is a great option when you want supporters to see the momentum building and compete openly for an item.

#### Blind Auction

A blind auction hides the current highest bid from supporters.

This means bidders place their bid based on what the item is worth to them, rather than simply increasing the current bid by the minimum amount.

Blind auctions can be a great fit for high-value items, unique experiences, or situations where you want bidders to submit more intentional offers.

#### Sealed Auction

A sealed auction is a type of blind auction where each bidder can submit only one bid.

Once submitted, the bid cannot be changed.

This format works well when you want supporters to submit their strongest bid upfront.

*** ** * ** ***

## How to Enable Auctions

To enable Auctions on your fundraiser:

1. Go to your fundraiser and log in.

2. Click **Manage Fundraiser**.

3. From the dashboard, click **Purchase Options**.

4. Click **Auctions**.

5. Toggle **Enable auctions** to **On**.

6. Click **Save**.

Once Auctions are enabled, you can set your auction dates, configure anti-sniping, and start building your item list.

If you do not see **Auctions** under **Purchase Options**, please contact your CrowdChange representative to confirm whether Auctions are enabled on your site.

*** ** * ** ***

### Set Your Auction Schedule

![image-20260501-174557.png](../assets/auctions-how-to-host-an-auction-on-crowdchange/image-20260501-174557.png)

Your auction schedule determines when bidding opens and closes.

You can set:

#### Start Date

This is when bidding opens for your auction.

#### End Date

This is when bidding closes for your auction.

These dates apply to all auction items by default. You can also set different dates on individual items if you want certain items to open or close at different times.

#### Anti-sniping

Anti-sniping helps keep the final moments of your auction fair, active, and exciting.

The number entered in the **Anti-sniping** field creates a final bidding window. If a bid is placed within that timeframe, the auction end time is extended by the same number of minutes.

For example, if your auction is set to end at **8:00 PM** and anti-sniping is set to **10 minutes** , a bid placed at **7:55 PM** will extend the auction to **8:05 PM**.

If another bid is placed at **8:02 PM** , the auction extends again to **8:12 PM**.

This helps prevent last-second bidding and gives other supporters a fair chance to respond, keeping the excitement going right until the true final bid.

*** ** * ** ***

## How to Set Up an Item

Each auction item is its own opportunity to inspire supporters. A strong title, clear description, great image, and thoughtful starting bid can make a big difference in how much attention and activity an item receives.

To create a new auction item:

1. Go to your fundraiser and log in.

2. Click **Manage Fundraiser**.

3. Click **Purchase Options**.

4. Click **Auctions**.

5. Click **Create item**.

6. Complete the item details.

7. Click **Save**.

Once saved, the item will use your main auction schedule unless you set custom dates for that specific item.

*** ** * ** ***

### Item Details

This is where you introduce the item and make it shine.

#### Item Name

Enter the name of the item as it should appear to supporters.

Examples:

* Signed Team Jersey

* Weekend Getaway Package

* VIP Event Experience

* Local Favourites Gift Basket

#### Description

Use the description to help supporters understand why the item is worth bidding on.

A great description can build excitement and answer important questions before someone places a bid.

Consider including:

* What is included

* Any restrictions or expiry dates

* Pickup, delivery, or shipping details

* Donor or sponsor recognition

* What makes the item special

* The impact of bidding on this item

For example, instead of writing "Dinner gift card," you might write:

"Enjoy a special night out with a $200 gift card to one of our favorite local restaurants, generously donated in support of this campaign. Perfect for a date night, celebration, or well-deserved treat."

**Suggested screenshot placement: Screenshot 5**

Place the first item setup screenshot here, showing **Item name** , **Description** , and the start of the **Bidding** section.

*** ** * ** ***

### Bidding Settings

This section controls how supporters can bid on the item.

#### Starting Bid

This is the first bid amount for the item.

For example, if the starting bid is $50, the first bidder must bid at least $50.

A thoughtful starting bid can help encourage early activity. For many items, it may be helpful to choose an amount that feels approachable while still reflecting the value of the item.

#### Bid Increment

This is the minimum amount each new bid must increase by.

For example, if the current bid is $100 and the bid increment is $25, the next minimum bid will be $125.

Bid increments help keep the auction moving. Smaller increments may encourage more bidding activity, while larger increments may be better suited for higher-value items.

#### Enable Buy Now

Buy Now gives supporters the option to purchase an item immediately at a set price.

When Buy Now is used:

* The supporter's payment method is charged immediately.

* The item closes.

* No further bids can be placed on that item.

Buy Now is a great option when you have a clear target price in mind, or when you want to give supporters the chance to secure a popular item right away.

*** ** * ** ***

### Auction Visibility Settings

These settings help shape the bidding experience for each item.

#### Blind Auction

A blind auction hides the current highest bid from supporters.

When Blind Auction is enabled:

* Supporters cannot see the current highest bid.

* Supporters cannot see whether they are currently winning.

* Bid history is hidden.

* Supporters only see their own bid information.

This can encourage supporters to bid based on the true value of the item to them, rather than only bidding slightly above the current amount.

#### Show Bidding History

For regular auctions, you can choose whether to show bidding history.

When enabled, supporters can view previous bids on the item details page.

When disabled, supporters will not see the full bidding history.

Please note that bidding history is never shown for blind auctions.

#### Sealed Auction

A sealed auction is a blind auction where each supporter can submit only one bid.

Once their bid has been submitted, it cannot be changed.

This creates a "best offer" style experience where every bidder has one chance to submit their strongest bid.

Please note that Sealed Auction can only be used with Blind Auction.

*** ** * ** ***

### Item Schedule

Each auction item can follow your main auction schedule, or have its own custom start and end dates.

Leave the item schedule blank if you want the item to use your general auction dates.

Set custom dates if you want an item to open or close at a different time.

This can be useful if you want to:

* Feature certain items for a limited time

* Launch new items throughout your campaign

* Keep high-value items open longer

* Create special bidding windows during an event

*** ** * ** ***

### Images

Upload images that help supporters quickly understand and get excited about the item.

Strong visuals can make your auction page feel more polished and engaging, especially when supporters are browsing multiple items.

Supported file types include:

* PNG

* JPG

* JPEG

* WEBP

*** ** * ** ***

### Additional Item Details

#### Expense

If tax receipts are enabled for auction purchases, use the **Expense** field to enter the portion of the item that is not eligible for an automated tax receipt.

For example, if an item sells for $300 and $100 should not be eligible for a tax receipt, enter $100 in the Expense field.

Please confirm your organization's receipting practices before launching your auction.

#### Fair Market Value

Enter the fair market value of the item.

This is the actual value of the item and may be used for display and reporting purposes.

#### Custom Code

Use this field for internal reporting or tracking.

For example, you may enter a SKU, package number, donor reference, or internal item code.

This code is not shown to supporters.

*** ** * ** ***

### Tips for Building a Strong Auction Item

A great auction item does more than list the details. It helps supporters imagine the experience, understand the value, and feel excited to participate.

To get the most out of each item:

* Use clear, high-quality images.

* Write descriptions that feel engaging and complete.

* Include pickup, delivery, shipping, or fulfillment details.

* Set a starting bid that encourages early participation.

* Choose a bid increment that matches the value of the item.

* Use Buy Now for items with a strong fixed value.

* Consider blind or sealed bidding for unique or high-value items.

* Promote standout items before the auction opens.

* Remind supporters when bidding is closing soon.

A strong auction item can become a mini-campaign of its own, giving supporters something specific and exciting to rally around.

*** ** * ** ***

## Bidder Actions \& Experience

Once your auction is live, supporters can browse, bid, save items, and stay connected through notifications.

This section explains what bidders can expect when participating in your auction.

*** ** * ** ***

### Browsing Auction Items

Supporters can view all available auction items from the fundraiser's auction page.

Depending on your item settings, supporters may see:

* Item name

* Image

* Status, such as Live or Closed

* Time remaining

* Current bid

* Number of bids

* Buy Now option, if enabled

* Saved items

* Items they have already bid on

This makes it easy for supporters to explore what is available, return to their favourite items, and stay involved throughout the campaign.

*** ** * ** ***

### Viewing an Individual Item

Supporters can click into an auction item to see more details before placing a bid.

Depending on your settings, the item page may show:

* Item image

* Item description

* Current bid

* Number of bids

* Time remaining

* Starting bid

* Bid increment

* Minimum bid

* Fair market value

* Buy Now price, if enabled

* Bid history, if enabled

This gives supporters the information they need to bid confidently.

**Suggested screenshot placement: Screenshot 2**

Place the individual auction item screenshot here to show what a bidder sees when reviewing an item.

*** ** * ** ***

### Logging In Before Bidding

To place a bid, supporters must log in to their CrowdChange account.

If a supporter tries to bid while logged out, they will be prompted to log in or create an account before continuing.

This ensures each bid is connected to a valid user account.

*** ** * ** ***

### Adding a Payment Method

Before placing a bid, supporters must add a valid payment method to their account.

If they do not already have a payment method saved, they will be prompted to add one before their bid can be submitted.

This helps create a smoother checkout experience when the auction closes, since winning bids are charged automatically.  
![image-20260501-174810.png](../assets/auctions-how-to-host-an-auction-on-crowdchange/image-20260501-174810.png)

*** ** * ** ***

### Placing a Bid

Once logged in and once a payment method has been added, supporters can bid on live auction items.

Supporters may be able to:

* Click the automatic next bid button

* Enter a custom bid amount

* Use Buy Now, if enabled

* Save items they want to follow

* View items they have bid on

The automatic next bid is based on the current bid plus the bid increment.

For example, if the current bid is $100 and the bid increment is $25, the next minimum bid is $125.

All bids are final and cannot be cancelled by the bidder.

*** ** * ** ***

### Saved Items and My Bids

Supporters can save items they are interested in and view items they have already bid on.

This makes it easier for bidders to return to the auction, follow their favorite items, and jump back in when the competition heats up.

*** ** * ** ***

### Bidder Notifications

Supporters can configure auction notifications from their settings.

Notifications may be available by:

* Email

* SMS, if configured

Supporters can receive notifications when:

* They place a bid

* They are outbid

* They win an auction item

These notifications help keep bidders engaged and encourage them to return when there is new activity on an item they care about.

*** ** * ** ***

### How Bidders Are Charged

Bidders are not charged when they place a standard bid.

Instead, their payment method is charged if they win the item when the auction closes.

#### If the bidder wins an item

Their saved payment method is automatically charged for the winning bid amount after the auction ends.

#### If the bidder uses Buy Now

Their saved payment method is charged immediately, and the item closes right away.

#### If the payment fails

The bidder will be notified and prompted to update their payment method. The fundraiser admin will also be notified so they can follow up if needed.

There is no "bid now, pay later" option. A valid payment method must be added before bidding.

*** ** * ** ***

### Important Notes for Bidders

* Bidders must log in before placing a bid.

* Bidders must have a payment method on file before bidding.

* Bids are final and cannot be cancelled by the bidder.

* Standard bids are only charged if the bidder wins.

* Buy Now purchases are charged immediately.

* Winning bids are charged automatically when the auction closes.

* Covered fees do not apply to auction purchases, so the bidder pays the exact winning bid or Buy Now amount.

================================================================================

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/how-to-create-and-share-an-instagram-image-sharing | Nav: How to Create and Share an Instagram Image - Sharing your CrowdChange page or fundraiser via Instagram | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# How to Create and Share an Instagram Image - Sharing your CrowdChange page or fundraiser via Instagram

The Instagram Share feature allows participants to create custom images for Instagram Stories, Posts, and other formats, making it easier to promote their fundraising page and encourage donations. This feature is available from the **Share** block on fundraising, personal fundraising, and team fundraising pages.

## Step 1: Open the Share Menu

1. Navigate to your fundraising page, personal fundraising page, or team fundraising page.

2. Scroll to the **Share** block.

3. Click the **Instagram** icon.

You will be taken to the **Create your share image** screen.  
![image-20260603-183014.png](../assets/how-to-create-and-share-an-instagram-image-sharing/image-20260603-183014.png)

*** ** * ** ***

## Step 2: Choose Your Image Type

Select how you would like to create your Instagram image. Each option will generate a share-ready image that can include key fundraising details such as the fundraiser name, amount raised, number of donors, fundraising goal, and a link sticker placeholder for Instagram Stories.  
![image-20260603-182626.png](../assets/how-to-create-and-share-an-instagram-image-sharing/image-20260603-182626.png)

### Campaign Images

Choose from existing campaign images already uploaded to the fundraiser. This is a great option when your organization already has branded graphics available.

### Use My Own Image

Use an image from your own device or camera roll to create a personalized share image. This can help create a more personal fundraising appeal.

### Transparent

Start with a blank slate using a transparent background.

### QR Code

Create a QR code image for sharing. This option can be used to help supporters quickly access your fundraising page by scanning the QR code.  
![image-20260603-183421.png](../assets/how-to-create-and-share-an-instagram-image-sharing/image-20260603-183421.png)

*** ** * ** ***

## Step 3: Crop and Format Your Image

If you select **Campaign Images** or **Use My Own Image**, you will be prompted to crop your image.

Choose the format you would like to create:

* Story

* Post (Landscape)

* Post (Portrait)

* Square

Adjust the crop area as needed, then click **Done**.  
![image-20260603-183109.png](../assets/how-to-create-and-share-an-instagram-image-sharing/image-20260603-183109.png)

*** ** * ** ***

## Step 4: Generate Your Share Image

Once your image has been cropped and formatted, CrowdChange will generate a share-ready image containing fundraising information such as:

* Fundraiser name

* Amount raised

* Number of donors

* Fundraising goal

* Link sticker placeholder (for Instagram Stories)

Review the generated image before sharing.  
![image-20260603-183145.png](../assets/how-to-create-and-share-an-instagram-image-sharing/image-20260603-183145.png)

*** ** * ** ***

## Step 5: Share Your Image

You have two options for sharing your image:

### Option 1: Share Directly

1. Click **Share to Instagram**.

2. Select **Instagram** from your device's sharing menu.

3. Follow Instagram's prompts to create your post or story.

### Option 2: Save the Image

1. Press and hold the generated image.

2. Save it to your device.

3. Upload it manually to Instagram at any time.

![IMG_4051-20260603-172242.jpg](../assets/how-to-create-and-share-an-instagram-image-sharing/IMG_4051-20260603-172242.jpg)

*** ** * ** ***

## Important: Adding a Link Sticker to Instagram Stories

When sharing to **Instagram Stories**, CrowdChange cannot automatically add a clickable link sticker due to Instagram's platform restrictions.

If you want supporters to be able to visit your fundraising page directly from your Story, you must manually add Instagram's **Link Sticker** before publishing.

To do this:

1. Create your share image and select **Share to Instagram**.

2. Choose **Instagram Stories** when prompted.

3. Once the Story opens in Instagram, tap the **Sticker** icon.

4. Select **Link**.

5. Paste your fundraising page URL into the Link Sticker.

6. Position the sticker over the **"Paste link sticker here"** placeholder shown on the generated image.

7. Publish your Story.

**Please Note:** The "Paste link sticker here" area on the generated image is only a visual placeholder. The link sticker is not added automatically and must be inserted manually within Instagram before posting. If a link sticker is not added, viewers will not have a direct way to access your fundraising page from the Story.

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/community-feed-block-how-to-share-updates-on-your- | Nav: Community Feed Block - How to share updates on your fundraiser, team or personal fundraising page | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# Community Feed Block - How to share updates on your fundraiser, team or personal fundraising page

The Community Feed is a social engagement feature that allows fundraiser owners, team captains, and personal page owners to share updates, celebrate achievements, and engage with supporters directly on their fundraising pages.

Community Feed helps keep supporters informed throughout a campaign by making it easy to post updates, share photos and videos, celebrate fundraising milestones, and encourage ongoing participation.  
![image-20260609-145142.png](../assets/community-feed-block-how-to-share-updates-on-your-/image-20260609-145142.png)
*The Community Feed allows page owners to share updates, media, and milestones while keeping supporters engaged throughout their fundraising journey.*

*** ** * ** ***

## Creating a Post

Page owners can create and publish updates directly from the Community Feed section.

### To create a post:

1. Navigate to your Fundraiser, Team, or Personal Fundraising Page.

2. Locate the **Community Feed** block.

3. Enter your message in the text field.

4. Optionally add media or a milestone.

5. Select any additional options:

   * Hide comments

   * Pin post

6. Click **Post**.

![image-20260609-145345.png](../assets/community-feed-block-how-to-share-updates-on-your-/image-20260609-145345.png)
*Enter your update directly into the Community Feed composer before posting.*

*** ** * ** ***

## Adding Images, GIFs, and Videos

Community Feed posts can include media to make updates more engaging and visually appealing.

Depending on your site's configuration, page owners may be able to add:

### Images

Upload photos from your device to share event updates, fundraising progress, thank-you messages, or campaign highlights.

### GIFs

Add GIFs to celebrate milestones, thank donors, or create fun and engaging updates.  
![image-20260609-145523.png](../assets/community-feed-block-how-to-share-updates-on-your-/image-20260609-145523.png)
*GIFs can be added to make Community Feed updates more engaging and celebratory.*

### Videos

Share video content to tell your story, provide campaign updates, or thank supporters.  
![image-20260609-145612.png](../assets/community-feed-block-how-to-share-updates-on-your-/image-20260609-145612.png)
*Videos from YouTube, Vimeo, or Twitch can be added via the* ***Video*** *button*

*** ** * ** ***

## Milestone Posts

Community Feed includes milestone-sharing functionality that helps page owners celebrate fundraising achievements.

When a page reaches certain fundraising milestones, CrowdChange may display a suggested post that can be shared with a single click.

Examples include:

* Reaching a fundraising amount goal

* Reaching a donation count milestone

* Earning an Activity Tracker badge

Page owners can choose to:

* Share the milestone immediately

* Dismiss the suggestion

If dismissed, the same milestone prompt will not continue to appear repeatedly.  
![image-20260609-145735.png](../assets/community-feed-block-how-to-share-updates-on-your-/image-20260609-145735.png)
*When a milestone is reached, page owners can quickly share their achievement with supporters.*

*** ** * ** ***

## Following a Page

Supporters can follow Fundraiser, Team, and Personal Pages to stay informed about future updates.

### Registered Users

Logged-in users can click **Follow Page** and automatically receive Community Feed notifications using the email address associated with their account.

### Anonymous Visitors

Visitors who do not have a CrowdChange account can subscribe to updates using their email address or SMS notifications (if enabled).  
![image-20260609-145831.png](../assets/community-feed-block-how-to-share-updates-on-your-/image-20260609-145831.png)
*Supporters can follow a page to receive future Community Feed updates and notifications.*

*** ** * ** ***

## Notifications

When a new Community Feed post is published:

* Followers receive a notification about the update.

* Email notifications include a direct link back to the page.

* Followers can unsubscribe at any time.

* Users can manage their notification preferences within their CrowdChange profile settings.

*** ** * ** ***

## Comments and Reactions

Community Feed is designed to encourage supporter engagement.

### Reactions

Supporters can react to posts and comments.

Anonymous visitors may react without creating an account.

### Comments

Supporters can comment on Community Feed posts to show encouragement and interact with page owners.

Please note:

* Commenting requires a registered CrowdChange account.

* Comments are subject to spam and profanity filtering.

* Site administrators may disable comments entirely.

![image-20260609-145935.png](../assets/community-feed-block-how-to-share-updates-on-your-/image-20260609-145935.png)
*Supporters can engage with Community Feed posts through reactions and comments.*

*** ** * ** ***

## Pinning Posts

Page owners can pin important posts to keep them visible at the top of the Community Feed.

Pinned posts are ideal for:

* Campaign announcements

* Event reminders

* Fundraising challenges

* Sponsor acknowledgements

* Thank-you messages

To pin a post, select **Pin Post** before publishing.

*** ** * ** ***

## Community Feed Configuration (Admins)

Administrators can customize the appearance and functionality of the Community Feed block through the Fundraiser Design Editor.

### Available Configuration Options

#### Appearance Settings

* Block title

* Title alignment

* Background colour

* Accent colour

* Background image

* Mobile background image

* Background opacity

* Title text colour

#### Content Controls

* Allow comments

* Allow images

* Allow videos

* Allow GIFs

#### Page-Specific Settings

Separate Community Feed settings can be configured for:

* Team Pages

* Personal Pages

This allows administrators to control which Community Feed features are available across different page types.  
![image-20260609-181501.png](../assets/community-feed-block-how-to-share-updates-on-your-/image-20260609-181501.png)
*Administrators can customize both the appearance and functionality of the Community Feed block.*

*** ** * ** ***

## Best Practices

We recommend posting regularly throughout your campaign to keep supporters engaged.

Popular Community Feed content includes:

* Fundraising progress updates

* Donor thank-you messages

* Event photos

* Team achievements

* Activity Tracker accomplishments

* Milestone celebrations

* Calls to action encouraging donations or participation

Frequent updates help maintain momentum and encourage supporters to return to your page throughout the campaign.

================================================================================

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/how-to-add-or-change-an-avatar-on-a-personal-or-te | Nav: How to Add or Change an Avatar on a Personal or Team Fundraising Page | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# How to Add or Change an Avatar on a Personal or Team Fundraising Page

Personal and Team Fundraising Pages now support Avatars, allowing page owners to display a profile-style image that represents themselves or their team.

Avatars are displayed within the **Cover image block**and help personalize fundraising pages.

*** ** * ** ***

## **Avatar and Cover Image Display**

Fundraiser owners can enable the Avatar layout for Personal and Team Fundraising Pages and customize how it appears.

**How to Enable the Avatar Layout**

1. Navigate to your fundraiser and click **Manage Fundraiser**.

2. Click **Design Your Fundraiser**.

3. Click **Edit** in the top right corner of the Hero image section.

4. Under **Team and personal pages** select the **Avatar and Cover** layout.

5. Configure the desired settings and click **Save**.

![image-20260612-124725.png](../assets/how-to-add-or-change-an-avatar-on-a-personal-or-te/image-20260612-124725.png)
Select the Avatar \& Cover layout under Team and Personal Pages.

*** ** * ** ***

## **Available Configurations**

Once enabled, you can:

* Upload a dedicated cover image for Personal and Team Pages.

* Allow page owners to change the cover image on their own page.

* Select the background color for the avatar section.

* Select the text color used within the avatar section.

![image-20260612-124823.png](../assets/how-to-add-or-change-an-avatar-on-a-personal-or-te/image-20260612-124823.png)
Customize the cover image, permissions, and colours for Personal and Team Pages.

*** ** * ** ***

## **Cover Image Behavior**

When a dedicated cover image is uploaded, it will be displayed on all Personal and Team Fundraising pages.

If no dedicated cover image is uploaded, the fundraiser's main hero image will automatically be used as the default cover image on all Personal and Team Fundraising pages.

*** ** * ** ***

## **Changing Your Avatar**

You can update your avatar at any time from your Personal or Team Fundraising Page.

1. Go to your Personal or Team Fundraising Page and log in.

2. Hover your cursor over the avatar image.

3. Click the **pencil icon** that appears on the avatar or click directly on the avatar image.

4. A file selection window will open on your device.

5. Select the image you would like to use and upload it.

6. Adjust the image if prompted and click **Save**.

![image-20260612-124925.png](../assets/how-to-add-or-change-an-avatar-on-a-personal-or-te/image-20260612-124925.png)

Your new avatar will be displayed immediately after saving.

This can also be adjusted within your Personal or Team Page Settings.

*** ** * ** ***

## **For Personal Pages**

1. Go to your Personal Fundraising Page and log in.

2. Click **Manage My Page**.

3. Select **Page Settings**.

4. Locate the **Image \& Video** section.

5. Click **Upload Image**.

6. Select an image from your computer.

7. Adjust the image and click **Save**.

8. Click **Save** at the bottom of the page settings screen.

![image-20260612-125025.png](../assets/how-to-add-or-change-an-avatar-on-a-personal-or-te/image-20260612-125025.png)
Update your avatar at any time from your page settings.

*** ** * ** ***

## **For Team Pages**

1. Go to your Team Fundraising Page and log in.

2. Click **Manage My Team**.

3. Select **Team Settings**.

4. Locate the **Image \& Video** section.

5. Click **Upload** or **Change Avatar**.

6. Select an image from your computer.

7. Adjust the image if prompted and click **Save**.

8. Click **Save** at the bottom of the page settings screen.

*** ** * ** ***

## **Team Avatar Display Logic**

When a Team Fundraising Page is created, the system will automatically determine which avatar to display based on the images that have been provided.

* If a team avatar is uploaded during the Create a Team process, that image will be displayed as the Team Page avatar.

* If no team avatar is uploaded, the Team Captain's avatar will automatically be used as the Team Page avatar.

* If the Team Captain does not upload an avatar when creating their Personal Fundraising Page, their profile image will be used as the avatar for both their Personal Fundraising Page and the Team Fundraising Page.

This ensures that every Team Fundraising Page will have an avatar displayed, even if a dedicated team image has not been uploaded.

*** ** * ** ***

## **Tips for Best Results**

* Use a high-quality square image whenever possible.

* Avoid images with important content near the edges.

* Ensure the subject is centered for the best appearance across devices.

* Use clear logos or group photos for team avatars.

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/pay-by-installments-how-to-break-a-donation-up-into-separate-payments | Nav: Pay by Installments - how to break a donation up into separate payments | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# Pay by Installments - how to break a donation up into separate payments

**Pay by Installments** allows donors to commit to a single donation amount and spread the payment over a fixed number of monthly installments.

Unlike recurring donations, installments represent one donation commitment that is paid overtime. The donor makes one pledge for the full amount, and the remaining payments are automatically collected on the selected schedule.

**Enabling Pay by Installments**

**Please Note:** Pay by Installments is an optional feature that must first be enabled for your organization.

Once enabled, administrators can configure these settings within the Fundraiser's Donations settings.

To turn on Pay by installments within a fundraiser, please follow the steps below:

1. **Login** to the fundraiser

<!-- -->

2. Click **Manage fundraiser** in the top right corner

<!-- -->

3. Click **Donation settings** in the menu on the left

<!-- -->

4. Scroll to **Pay by installments** and toggle on **Accept installment donations**

<!-- -->

5. Set the **Installment duration** and **Payment schedule options**

<!-- -->

6. Scroll down and click **Save**

![image-20260707-125714.png](../assets/pay-by-installments-how-to-break-a-donation-up-into-separate-payments/image-20260707-125714.png)
Pay by installments settings within Donation settings

*** ** * ** ***

**Donor Checkout Experience**

The Pay by Installments option is only displayed when all of the following conditions are met:

* Pay by Installments is enabled for the fundraiser.

* The donor selects a **One-Time** donation.

* The donation amount is greater than $0.

If multiple options are available, donors can choose:

* **Pay Now** or **Pay by Installments**

* The number of monthly payments

* Their preferred monthly payment date

Before completing checkout, donors will see a payment preview showing:

* Total donation amount

* Amount of each monthly payment

* Number of scheduled payments

The donation is then processed as a single pledged donation with an installment schedule attached.  
![image-20260707-125651.png](../assets/pay-by-installments-how-to-break-a-donation-up-into-separate-payments/image-20260707-125651.png)
View of Pay in installments option on the Checkout Page

*** ** * ** ***

**How Payments Work**

When a donor selects Pay by Installments:

1. The donor's full donation commitment (pledge) is created immediately.

2. The first installment is charged immediately using the selected payment method.

3. The payment method is securely stored for future scheduled payments.

4. Remaining installments are automatically charged on the selected monthly schedule.

5. Once all scheduled payments have been successfully collected, the installment plan is completed automatically.

Unlike recurring donations, installment plans are **not subscriptions**. They are a single donation commitment that is fulfilled through multiple scheduled payments.

*** ** * ** ***

**Fundraiser Status**

Once a donor commits to an installment plan, the payment schedule will continue even if the fundraiser has been:

* Closed

* Archived

* Ended

This ensures donors can complete the commitment they originally made.

*** ** * ** ***

**Donation Receipts**

After each successful installment payment, the donor receives a payment receipt showing their current progress.

Receipt summaries include:

* Amount paid

* Total pledged amount

* Remaining balance

* Number of payments completed

* Total number of scheduled payments

* Date of the next scheduled payment (when applicable)

If there are no remaining scheduled payments, the receipt will indicate that the installment plan has been completed.

**Please Note:** If you use a custom receipt template that does not include the transaction summary, the installment progress section will automatically be added to the donor receipt.

*** ** * ** ***

**Reporting**

For reporting purposes, the **original pledge** represents the donation.

The individual monthly payments are treated as fulfilments of that pledge and are not counted as separate donations.

This ensures donation totals, fundraising progress, donor counts, and leaderboards remain accurate without double-counting payments.

Administrators can view installment progress, including:

* Total pledge amount

* Amount collected

* Remaining balance

* Percentage completed

* Number of payments completed

* Total scheduled payments

* Next scheduled payment

* Saved card details (brand, last four digits, and expiry)

Transaction details also provide links between the original pledge and all associated installment payments, making it easy to review the complete payment history.

*** ** * ** ***

**Managing Installment Plans**

If an installment payment fails, administrators can:

* View the reason for the failed payment.

* Update the donor's saved payment method.

* Retry the missed payment.

* Close the installment plan at the amount already collected if no further payments will be processed.

*** ** * ** ***

**Refunds**

Refunds apply only to individual installment payments that have already been charged.

Refunding an installment payment does not automatically refund or remove the original pledge.

If an installment payment is refunded while the plan is still active:

* The donor's paid progress is reduced.

* Future scheduled payments continue as planned.

If a payment from a completed or already closed installment plan is refunded:

* The pledged amount is adjusted to match the amount successfully collected.

* The installment plan is marked as closed.

This ensures donation totals, fundraising reports, and donor leaderboards continue to accurately reflect the amount received.

*** ** * ** ***

**Frequently Asked Questions**

**Can donors change an installment plan after donating?**

No. Donors cannot modify the payment amount, payment schedule, or number of installments after the donation has been submitted. If changes are required, please contact your CrowdChange support team.

**Is Pay by Installments the same as recurring donations?**

No. Recurring donations create an ongoing monthly or annual subscription until cancelled.

Pay by Installments creates a single donation commitment that is automatically completed after the selected number of monthly payments have been collected.

**Will installment payments continue after my fundraiser ends?**

Yes. Existing installment plans continue until all scheduled payments have been completed, even if the fundraiser has been closed or archived.

**Do installment payments count as multiple donations?**

No. The original pledge is counted as the donation. Individual installment payments are recorded as fulfilments of that pledge and are excluded from donation totals and donor leaderboards to prevent double-counting.

================================================================================

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/multi-column-block-how-to-add-multiple-content-columns-to-the-body-of-your-fundraising-page | Nav: Multi-Column Block - How to add multiple content columns to the body of your fundraising page | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# Multi-Column Block - How to add multiple content columns to the body of your fundraising page

The Multi-Column Block allows you to add one, two, or three content columns directly within the body of your fundraiser page. This is a helpful way to organize information, highlight key campaign details, feature sponsors, share impact statements, or combine text and images in a clean layout.

Each column can be customized individually, allowing you to add text, images, titles, background colors, and styling to create a flexible content section that matches your fundraiser branding.  
![image-20260707-134516.png](../assets/multi-column-block-how-to-add-multiple-content-columns-to-the-body-of-your-fundraising-page/image-20260707-134516.png)
A view of the **Multi-column block**featuring three columns

*** ** * ** ***

## How to add a Multi-Column Block

The Multi-Column Block is not enabled by default. To add a Multi-Column Block, please follow these steps:

1. Go to your CrowdChange page and log in.

2. Once on the fundraiser you would like to edit, click **Design**.

3. Within the user interface, between any two blocks, click the Plus icon.

4. The list of available blocks will then be shown. Select the Multi-Column Block.

*** ** * ** ***

## Layout - how to choose the number of columns

Within the Layout section of the Multi-Column Block editor, you can choose how many columns should display in the block.

Available layout options include:

One - Displays one full-width column.

Two - Displays two columns side by side.

Three - Displays three columns side by side.

Once you select the number of columns, each column will appear in the Layout section as its own editable item, such as Column #1, Column #2, and Column #3. To edit the individual column settings/content, click the icons on the far right hand side of the Column box.  
![image-20260707-134724.png](../assets/multi-column-block-how-to-add-multiple-content-columns-to-the-body-of-your-fundraising-page/image-20260707-134724.png)
Layout settings within the multi-column block

*** ** * ** ***

## Appearance - how to adjust the overall block style

Within the Appearance section of the Multi-Column Block editor, you can customize the overall look of the full Multi-Column Block.

Available appearance settings include:

**Title text color** - Controls the colour of the main block title.

**Title alignment** - Controls whether the main block title is aligned left, right, centered, or hidden.

**Background color** - Controls the background colour behind the full Multi-Column Block.

**Background opacity** - Controls the transparency of the block background.

**Background image for desktop** - Allows you to upload a background image for the block.

*** ** * ** ***

## Content - how to set the block title

Within the Content section of the Multi-Column Block editor, you can update the main title for the full block.

If you do not want a title to appear above the block, you can hide the title using the Title alignment setting in the Appearance section.

*** ** * ** ***

## Column settings - how to edit each column

Each column within the Multi-Column Block has its own settings. To edit a column, click the column from the Layout section.

Within each column, you can customize:

**Column title** - Adds a title to the individual column.

**Text**- Allows you to edit the content displayed inside the column.

**Title text color**- Controls the colour of the individual column title.

**Background color** - Controls the background colour of the individual column.

**Background opacity** - Controls the transparency of the individual column background.

**Background image for desktop**- Allows you to upload a background image for that specific column.

**Darken background image** - Adds a dark overlay to the column background image, which can help make text easier to read.  
![image-20260707-134944.png](../assets/multi-column-block-how-to-add-multiple-content-columns-to-the-body-of-your-fundraising-page/image-20260707-134944.png)
Customization options within a column

To edit the main text or image content inside a column, click Edit content. This will allow you to add or update the content displayed in that specific column.

*** ** * ** ***

## Tips for using the Multi-Column Block

For best results, keep each column similar in length so the layout remains balanced.

Use clear, concise titles for each column.

If using images, try to use images with similar dimensions or aspect ratios.

If placing text over a background image, use the Darken background image option to improve readability.

Use the three-column layout for shorter content, such as feature highlights or sponsor recognition. Use the one or two-column layout for longer descriptions or larger images.

# Fundraiser cards - how to change the image on homepage, tickets, and preview

**Fundraiser cards**refer to the images shown on your CrowdChange homepage, smaller versions of your fundraiser's cover image at checkout, and the image shown on PDF tickets generated via CrowdChange. This image can be different from your main cover image. This is due to the differing dimensions/layout of these areas.

## How to change / update your **Fundraiser card**

Once you have created your fundraiser, please follow these steps to update your **Fundraiser card**.

* Go to your fundraiser and click **Dashboard**

* Once on the **fundraiser dashboard** , click **General settings**

* Then you will see the **Fundraiser card** section

* Click on your image to adjust this

The aspect ratio for fundraiser cards is 16:9.  
![image-20260812-141411.png](../assets/fundraiser-cards-how-to-change-the-image-on-homepage-tickets-and-preview/image-20260812-141411.png)

## Things to note

* When you initially create your fundraiser, the cover image uploaded during the **Start a fundraiser** process will be your fundraiser card

* Changes to your cover image post-creation, however, will not adjust the fundraiser card - the above steps must be taken

* Bilingual fundraisers will require separate images for English and French - however, the option to **Copy to French** will be there if an English image is uploaded

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/how-to-use-donation-encouragement-to-support-fundraising-goals | Nav: How to Use Donation Encouragement to Support Fundraising Goals | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# How to Use Donation Encouragement to Support Fundraising Goals

Donation Encouragement is an optional checkout feature that invites donors to increase their donation when an additional amount would help the applicable fundraiser, team, or personal fundraising page reach a higher percentage of its goal.

The prompt is optional. Donors can accept the suggested increase, keep their original donation amount, or close the prompt and continue with checkout.  
![image-20260812-171135.png](../assets/how-to-use-donation-encouragement-to-support-fundraising-goals/image-20260812-171135.png)
A view of **Donation encouragement** on a fundraiser with a goal of $1,000

## Before You Begin: Set a Fundraising Goal

A fundraising goal is required for Donation Encouragement to work. The feature uses the amount raised and the applicable goal to determine when a suggested increase can be shown.

For Donation Encouragement to work on a particular fundraiser, team, or personal fundraising page, that destination must have a goal set.

You can review or update goals in the following locations:

* **Main fundraiser:** Go to **Dashboard → General settings → Goal Measure Unit**.

* **Team fundraising page:** Go to **Team dashboard → Team Settings**.

* **Personal fundraising page:** Go to **Page dashboard → Page Settings**.

## How to Enable Donation Encouragement

1. Go to your CrowdChange site and log in.

2. Navigate to the fundraiser where you would like to enable Donation Encouragement.

3. Click **Dashboard**.

![image-20260812-171342.png](../assets/how-to-use-donation-encouragement-to-support-fundraising-goals/image-20260812-171342.png)

4. Select **Donation settings** from the menu on the left.

![image-20260812-171410.png](../assets/how-to-use-donation-encouragement-to-support-fundraising-goals/image-20260812-171410.png)

5. Click **Donation amounts \& types**.

6. Scroll down to the **Donation encouragement** section.

![image-20260812-171432.png](../assets/how-to-use-donation-encouragement-to-support-fundraising-goals/image-20260812-171432.png)

7. Toggle on **Donation encouragement**.

8. Under **Enable donation encouragement for donations made to**, select where the feature should apply:

   * **Fundraiser:** Enables Donation Encouragement for donations made directly to the main fundraiser.

   * **Teams:** Enables Donation Encouragement for donations made to team fundraising pages.

   * **Pages:** Enables Donation Encouragement for donations made to personal fundraising pages.

   These settings can be enabled or disabled separately.

![image-20260812-171500.png](../assets/how-to-use-donation-encouragement-to-support-fundraising-goals/image-20260812-171500.png)

9. Scroll to the bottom of the page and click **Save** to confirm your settings.

## How Donation Encouragement Works at Checkout

When a donor enters a donation amount, CrowdChange uses the applicable fundraising goal and current amount raised to determine whether an optional suggested increase can be shown.

For example, a donor enters a donation of **$125** . If an additional **$25** would bring the fundraiser to **15% of its goal**, the donor will see the following message:
> Just $25 from reaching 15% of our goal.

The donor can then choose one of the following options:

* Select **Add $25 to hit 15%** to increase the donation from $125 to $150.

* Select **Keep $125** to continue with the original donation amount.

* Select the **X** to close the prompt.

The donation amount will only increase if the donor selects the suggested increase.

## Additional Information

* A fundraising goal is required for the feature to provide a goal-based suggestion.

* The suggested amount and percentage will vary based on the applicable goal and current fundraising progress.

* The prompt may not appear for every donation amount.

* Donors are not required to accept the suggestion.

* The donor's original donation amount remains unchanged unless they select the suggested increase.

* The feature can be enabled independently for the main fundraiser, team pages, and personal fundraising pages.

last_modified: '2026-09-22T14:36:16.043Z'

word_count: 729

<!-- Source: https://chadmin.crowdchange.help/ct/how-global-inventory-works | Nav: How Global Inventory Works | Mirrored 2026-10-14 -->

# How Global Inventory Works

Global inventory allows your organization to use one shared stock pool across multiple fundraisers. It is designed for situations where the same physical inventory is sold through more than one fundraiser and every sale should draw from the same central supply.

For example, if several fundraisers sell the same t-shirt, hoodie, meal ticket, or merchandise item, global inventory helps prevent your organization from selling more than the total quantity available.

Each fundraiser still controls how the item appears to buyers, including its price, images, description, access code rules, and purchase limits. **Global inventory only controls the shared stock count.**

**Important:** Global inventory does not replace purchase options. Instead, it adds shared stock tracking to purchase options.

**When to Use Global Inventory**

Use global inventory when:

* The same item is sold across multiple fundraisers.

* The item comes from one central stock supply.

* Your organization needs to prevent overselling across fundraisers.

Global inventory may not be necessary when:

* The item is sold through only one fundraiser.

* Each fundraiser has its own separate stock.

* The item does not have a stock limit.

* You only need a per-fundraiser purchase limit.

**Link Global Inventory to Purchase Options**

Once global inventory has been set up, it can be linked to purchase options on a fundraiser or Blueprint.

How you link the inventory depends on whether the purchase option has variations.

**Purchase Options Without Variations**

Use this method when the purchase option represents one item and buyers do not select from different variations.

1. Open the purchase option.

2. Select **Global inventory** as the inventory source.

3. Select the appropriate global inventory item.

4. Select the matching variant.

5. Save the purchase option.

Once saved, purchases made through that fundraiser will reduce the stock for the selected global inventory variant.

**Purchase Options With Variations**

If buyers choose from variations such as size, colour, ticket type, or meal choice, each purchase option variation must be linked to its matching global inventory variant.

1. Open the purchase option.

2. Add or edit the purchase option variations.

3. Link each variation to the matching global inventory variant.

4. Save the purchase option.

**Important:** When a purchase option has variations, link global inventory to **each individual variation**, rather than only to the parent item.

For example:

**Fundraiser variation:** Small t-shirt

**Global inventory:** T-shirt / Small

**Fundraiser variation:** Medium t-shirt

**Global inventory:** T-shirt / Medium

**What Happens at Checkout**

When a buyer selects an item linked to global inventory, CrowdChange checks whether enough shared stock is available.

If sufficient stock is available, the buyer can continue through checkout. When the purchase is completed, the shared stock is updated automatically.

If the available stock changes before the purchase is completed, the buyer cannot purchase more than the quantity remaining.

This helps protect shared inventory when multiple fundraisers are selling from the same stock at the same time.

**What Happens When a Purchase Is Refunded or Rolled Back**

When a purchase linked to global inventory is refunded or rolled back, the shared inventory quantities are updated automatically.

This means the inventory associated with the refunded or rolled-back purchase is returned to the shared stock without requiring a manual inventory adjustment.

**Editing Inventory Links After Purchases**

After an item linked to global inventory has been purchased, some inventory settings may become locked. This helps protect purchase history and prevents inventory from being moved accidentally after sales have already occurred.

The linked inventory can still be viewed, but the inventory source or selected global inventory item may not be freely changed.

**Important:** If an inventory link needs to be changed after purchases have already been made, review the potential impact on existing purchases and inventory before making changes.

**What Happens When Linked Inventory Becomes Unavailable**

When global inventory is archived or deleted, it is no longer available for new inventory links. Existing links are preserved so previous purchases remain associated with the correct inventory.

If unavailable inventory is still linked to an active purchase option:

* A purchase option without variations may become unavailable for sale.

* For a purchase option with variations, the unavailable variation may be hidden.

* Other active variations can continue to be sold if they are still available.

If archived inventory is restored, it becomes available again. However, some linked purchase options may need to be reopened manually before buyers can purchase them again.

================================================================================
